title: MRN-ATM pathway activation and senescence-associated phenotype of CD4+ T cells in chronic hepatitis B
abstract: T-cell senescence is a hallmark of immune dysfunction in persistent viral infections, characterized by DNA damage accumulation and telomere attrition. However, the role of DNA damage response pathway in CD4 + T-cell senescence during chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains poorly defined. In this study, we demonstrated that people with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) exhibited senescence-associated phenotype in CD4 + T cells, marked by elevated KLRG1, along with increased DNA damage and telomere shortening, compared to healthy subjects (HS). Notably, activation of the MRE11/RAD50/NBS1-ataxia telangiectasia mutated (MRN-ATM) pathway was prominent in CD4 + T cells from CHB patients. Importantly, suppression of MRN attenuated ATM phosphorylation and its downstream signaling molecules, and inhibition of ATM reduced the production of IFN-γ and IL-2 in CD4 + T lymphocytes isolated from individuals with CHB and HS. Our findings indicate that during chronic HBV infection, CD4 + T cells exhibited senescence-associated phenotype, telomere shortening and genomic DNA damage. Concurrent activation of the MRN-ATM pathway may represent a mechanism that repairs DNA damage and be associated with CD4 + T-cell cytokine production, although it does not fully prevent senescence. Elucidating the relationship between CD4 + T-cell senescence-associated phenotype and the MRN-ATM pathway, helps to understand the mechanisms underlying HBV persistence and may inform future therapeutic strategies.

abstract_zh: T 细胞衰老是持续性病毒感染中免疫功能障碍的标志,其特征是 DNA 损伤积累和端粒磨损。然而,慢性乙型肝炎 病毒 (HBV) 感染期间 DNA 损伤反应途径在 CD4 + T 细胞衰老中的作用仍不清楚。在这项研究中,我们证明,与健康受试者 (HS) 相比,慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 患者在 CD4 + T 细胞中表现出衰老相关表型,其特征是 KLRG1 升高,同时 DNA 损伤增加和端粒缩短。值得注意的是,MRE11/RAD50/NBS1-共济失调毛细血管扩张突变 (MRN-ATM) 通路的激活在慢性乙型肝炎患者的 CD4 + T 细胞中很显着。重要的是,抑制 MRN 会减弱 ATM 磷酸化及其下游信号分子,并且抑制 ATM 会减少从 CHB 和 HS 个体中分离出的 CD4 + T 淋巴细胞中 IFN-γ 和 IL-2 的产生。我们的研究结果表明,在慢性 HBV 感染期间,CD4 + T 细胞表现出衰老相关表型、端粒缩短和基因组 DNA 损伤。MRN-ATM 通路的同时激活可能代表一种修复 DNA 损伤的机制,并与 CD4 + T 细胞细胞因子的产生相关,尽管它并不能完全预防衰老。阐明 CD4 + T 细胞衰老相关表型与 MRN-ATM 通路之间的关系,有助于了解 HBV 持续存在的机制,并可能为未来的治疗策略提供信息。

title: Effectiveness and Patient Experience of the HBVCare Smartphone App for Improving Short-Term Treatment Adherence in Chronic Hepatitis B: Randomized Controlled Trial (Preprint)
abstract: BACKGROUND Chronic hepatitis B requires long-term medication adherence to prevent severe liver complications. Randomized evidence on mobile health apps for this purpose is limited, particularly in Vietnam. OBJECTIVE This study aimed to evaluate whether adding the HBVCare smartphone app to standard care improves treatment adherence at 3 months among patients with chronic hepatitis B, and to identify factors associated with adherence and describe user experience. METHODS We conducted a multicenter, single-blind, parallel-group randomized controlled trial at two sites in Hanoi, Vietnam. Adults with chronic hepatitis B who were eligible for antiviral treatment were randomized 1:1 to the intervention group (HBVCare and standard care; n=51) or the control group (standard care; n=52). The co-primary outcomes were medication adherence at 3 months (a perfect score of 25 on the Medication Adherence Report Scale-5 [MARS-5]) and follow-up adherence (a clinic visit within ±7 days of the scheduled date, verified from clinic records). Participants were analyzed as randomized, restricted to those with 3-month outcome data (complete-case analysis). User experience was assessed with the UMUX-Lite scale. RESULTS Of 103 randomized participants, 76 (73.8%) had outcome data (intervention group: n=40; control group: n=36). Good medication adherence was higher in the intervention group than in the control group (34/40, 85% vs 20/36, 55.6%; risk difference 29.4%, 95% CI 9.8 to 49.1; P=.01). On-schedule follow-up did not differ significantly (20/40, 50% vs 14/36, 38.9%; risk difference 11.1%, 95% CI –11.1 to 33.3; P=.46). At 3 months, 20/40 (50%) of the intervention participants were still using the app. Continuers were not significantly younger than discontinuers (mean age 37.0, SD 6.9 years vs 43.1, SD 13.7 years; P=.09), and 28/40 (70%) participants rated usability as acceptable. CONCLUSIONS In this trial, adding HBVCare to standard care was associated with higher self-reported medication adherence at 3 months among participants with outcome data, but not with on-schedule follow-up, and half of the intervention participants stopped using the app. Interpretation is limited by loss to follow-up, a self-reported outcome, and short follow-up. Longer trials with objective adherence measures are needed. CLINICALTRIAL ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07540637

title: Defining the Structure-Activity Relationships of Thiazolide Antivirals: Balancing Potency, Metabolic Stability, and Aqueous Solubility.
abstract: Recent studies on thiazolide antivirals have identified compounds RM5038 and RM5021 as potent inhibitors of hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and influenza A, although their development has been limited by poor aqueous solubility and rapid metabolic clearance. In this work, a series of novel halogen-substituted and 4'-alkylsulfone thiazolide analogs were synthesized using updated convergent synthetic approaches and flexible protecting group strategies. DMPK evaluation demonstrated that 3-X halogen substitution significantly improved aqueous solubility in parallel to enhancing metabolic stability. Within the chlorothiazolide series, compounds 10gand 10l displayed much improved metabolic stability profiles, excellent aqueous solubility representing a 10-fold improvement over the parent drug, together with low single-digit micromolar antiviral (influenza A) activity and acceptable in vitro safety indices. Evaluation of the 4'-alkylsulfone thiazolides also revealed improved in vitro DMPK profiles while retaining micromolar antiviral potency. SAR analysis indicated that short alkyl sulfone substituents containing two to three carbons are optimal for antiviral activity, while branched alkyl groups may provide additional metabolic advantages. In summary, compounds 10g, 10l, and 15d represent promising early leads for progression to in vivo profiling and additional preclinical evaluation.

title_zh: 定义噻唑化物 抗病毒药物 的结构-活性关系:平衡效力、代谢稳定性和水溶性。
source_body_en: Recent studies on thiazolide antivirals have identified compounds RM5038 and RM5021 as potent inhibitors of hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and influenza A, although their development has been limited by poor aqueous solubility and rapid metabolic clearance. In this work, a series of novel halogen-substituted and 4'-alkylsulfone thiazolide analogs were synthesized using updated convergent synthetic approaches and flexible protecting group strategies. DMPK evaluation demonstrated that 3-X halogen substitution significantly improved aqueous solubility in parallel to enhancing metabolic stability. Within the chlorothiazolide series, compounds 10gand 10l displayed much improved metabolic stability profiles, excellent aqueous solubility representing a 10-fold improvement over the parent drug, together with low single-digit micromolar antiviral (influenza A) activity and acceptable in vitro safety indices. Evaluation of the 4'-alkylsulfone thiazolides also revealed improved in vitro DMPK profiles while retaining micromolar antiviral potency. SAR analysis indicated that short alkyl sulfone substituents containing two to three carbons are optimal for antiviral activity, while branched alkyl groups may provide additional metabolic advantages. In summary, compounds 10g, 10l, and 15d represent promising early leads for progression to in vivo profiling and additional preclinical evaluation.

title: Hepatitis B and C burden and HCV care cascade among transgender women and men who have sex with men in an integrated one-stop shop model in Lahore and Larkana, Pakistan
abstract: Pakistan bears one of the highest global burdens of viral hepatitis, yet data on hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) among transgender women and men who have sex with men (MSM) remains limited. This study assessed Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and anti-HCV positivity among MSM and transgender women attending CBOs and described the HCV care cascade within an integrated one-stop-shop model. A prospective implementation study was conducted from October 2019 to October 2021 in Lahore, Punjab, and Larkana, Sindh. A total of 2,241 participants were enrolled through three community-based organizations (CBOs). The one-stop-shop model integrated HBV/HCV screening with CBO-coordinated HCV RNA confirmation, treatment, and follow-up within existing Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)/ Sexually transmitted infection (STI) services. Participants were screened using the Determine HBsAg rapid diagnostic test and the SD BIOLINE HCV antibody rapid diagnostic test, manufactured by Abbott Diagnostics. Anti-HCV-reactive participants underwent confirmatory HCV RNA testing using GeneXpert at designated laboratories coordinated through CBOs. HBsAg-positive participants were linked to public-sector hepatitis facilities. Treatment completion was defined as completion of the prescribed antiviral course, while sustained virological response (SVR) was used to assess HCV cure following treatment. Screening and care outcomes were compared between MSM and transgender women. Among 2,241 participants, 1,160 (51.9%) were MSM and 1,081 (48.1%) were transgender women. Overall HBsAg positivity was 3.1% and anti-HCV positivity was 8.9%. HBsAg positivity was higher among MSM than transgender women (4.9% versus 1.1%), as was anti-HCV positivity (13.4% versus 4.3%; p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, sharing razors/blades and toothbrushes were independently associated with higher odds of anti-HCV positivity. Of 201 anti-HCV-reactive participants, 159 (79.1%) underwent confirmatory HCV RNA testing, of whom 99 had detectable HCV RNA. Among these, 92 initiated HCV treatment, 74 completed treatment and 67 achieved SVR. Treatment completion did not differ significantly between MSM and transgender women (p = 0.264). All 69 HBsAg-positive participants were linked to public-sector hepatitis facilities for further management. CBO-based HIV/STI programmes can provide an important entry point for hepatitis care among MSM and transgender women and offer a practical approach to extending screening, diagnosis and treatment to key populations in Pakistan.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the burden of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) among men who have sex with men (MSM) and transgender women in Lahore and Larkana, Pakistan, using an integrated one-stop-shop model. A total of 2,241 participants were enrolled through community-based organizations (CBOs), with 51.9% being MSM and 48.1% transgender women. HBV and HCV screening was conducted using rapid diagnostic tests, and confirmatory HCV RNA testing was performed via GeneXpert. The study found that HBV and HCV positivity rates were higher among MSM compared to transgender women, with anti-HCV positivity being significantly associated with sharing razors and toothbrushes. Of the 201 anti-HCV-reactive participants, 79.1% underwent confirmatory testing, and 67 achieved sustained virological response (SVR) after treatment. The findings suggest that CBO-based HIV/STI programs can serve as a critical platform for hepatitis care in key populations. The study highlights the importance of integrated models for improving screening, diagnosis, and treatment access for HBV and HCV in Pakistan.

title: A Cross-Sectional Questionnaire-Based Study to Assess Knowledge, Attitude and Practice Regarding Needle Stick Injury and PostExposure Prophylaxis among Healthcare Workers in a Tertiary Care Teaching Hospital
abstract: Background: Needle stick injuries (NSIs) are a common occupational hazard among healthcare workers, with potential exposure to blood-borne pathogens such as human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), and hepatitis C virus (HCV). Despite the availability of standard precautions, hepatitis B vaccination, and postexposure prophylaxis (PEP), NSIs continue to occur due to unsafe practices, inadequate reporting, and gaps in postexposure management. Assessing healthcare workers’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices is therefore essential for identifying preventable gaps and strengthening occupational safety measures. Objective: To assess the knowledge, attitude and practices (KAP) regarding needle stick injuries and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) among healthcare workers in a tertiary-care teaching hospital. Methods: A hospital-based cross-sectional questionnaire study was conducted among 166 healthcare workers. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing demographic characteristics, knowledge regarding NSIs and PEP, attitudes towards occupational safety, and preventive and post-exposure practices. Knowledge was assessed using seven items, attitude using five Likert-scale statements, and practices using eight items. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and appropriate tests of association. Results: The study population had a mean age of 28.73 ± 6.88 years, with females comprising 67.5%. Overall knowledge regarding NSIs and PEP was good. 94.6% recognized transmission of HIV, HBV and HCV through NSIs, 97.6% identified washing with soap and water as the appropriate immediate first-aid measure, and 97.0% recognized needle recapping as unsafe. Attitudes were predominantly positive, with 93.4% considering NSI a serious occupational hazard and 95.8% supporting reporting of occupational exposures. However, 33.7% reported having experienced an NSI. Among those exposed, only 60.7% reported the injury and 57.1% received PEP. Although 98.8% reported appropriate sharps disposal, 46.4% reported always or sometimes recapping needles. Hepatitis B vaccination coverage was 92.8%.
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitude, and practices (KAP) of healthcare workers regarding needle stick injuries (NSIs) and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) in a tertiary-care teaching hospital. The cross-sectional questionnaire-based study included 166 participants with a mean age of 28.73 ± 6.88 years, where 67.5% were female. Knowledge about NSIs and PEP was found to be good, with 94.6% recognizing transmission of HIV, HBV, and HCV through NSIs, 97.6% identifying washing with soap and water as the appropriate first-aid measure, and 97.0% recognizing needle recapping as unsafe. title_zh: 一项基于横断面问卷的研究,旨在评估三级护理教学医院医护人员对针刺伤和暴露后预防的知识、态度和实践
source_body_en: Background: Needle stick injuries (NSIs) are a common occupational hazard among healthcare workers, with potential exposure to blood-borne pathogens such as human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), and hepatitis C virus (HCV). Despite the availability of standard precautions, hepatitis B vaccination, and postexposure prophylaxis (PEP), NSIs continue to occur due to unsafe practices, inadequate reporting, and gaps in postexposure management. Assessing healthcare workers’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices is therefore essential for identifying preventable gaps and strengthening occupational safety measures. Objective: To assess the knowledge, attitude and practices (KAP) regarding needle stick injuries and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) among healthcare workers in a tertiary-care teaching hospital. Methods: A hospital-based cross-sectional questionnaire study was conducted among 166 healthcare workers. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing demographic characteristics, knowledge regarding NSIs and PEP, attitudes towards occupational safety, and preventive and post-exposure practices. Knowledge was assessed using seven items, attitude using five Likert-scale statements, and practices using eight items. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and appropriate tests of association. Results: The study population had a mean age of 28.73 ± 6.88 years, with females comprising 67.5%. Overall knowledge regarding NSIs and PEP was good. 94.6% recognized transmission of HIV, HBV and HCV through NSIs, 97.6% identified washing with soap and water as the appropriate immediate first-aid measure, and 97.0% recognized needle recapping as unsafe. Attitudes were predominantly positive, with 93.4% considering NSI a serious occupational hazard and 95.8% supporting reporting of occupational exposures. However, 33.7% reported having experienced an NSI. Among those exposed, only 60.7% reported the injury and 57.1% received PEP. Although 98.8% reported appropriate sharps disposal, 46.4% reported always or sometimes recapping needles. Hepatitis B vaccination coverage was 92.8%.

title: Transfusion transmitted infection reactivity among blood donors in Botswana from 2020 to 2024: a retrospective study
abstract: Background Transfusion-transmissible infections (TTIs) remain an important threat to blood safety and require continuous surveillance among blood donors. Botswana National Blood Transfusion Services (NBTS) screens all donations for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and syphilis. We estimated TTI reactivity and assessed temporal and demographic associations among blood donors in Botswana. Methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of donation records from the Gaborone and Francistown NBTS sites between April 2020 and March 2025. The primary analysis used the first donation per donor-year. Annual reactive proportions and 95% Wilson confidence intervals were estimated. Population-averaged logistic regression with donor-clustered robust standard errors was used to estimate average annual change, and categorical-year models formally assessed departure from linearity. Analyses were conducted using Stata version 18. Results Among 102,102 source records from 61,446 donors, 34 same-day duplicate records and 1,138 later records from the 549 restored first-result-only donors were excluded. The final dataset contained 100,930 records from 61,439 donors and 84,303 donor-years. In continuous-year models, the average annual odds decreased for HCV (aOR 0.95, 95% CI 0.914–0.99), syphilis (aOR 0.92, 95% CI 0.88–0.95), and any TTI (aOR 0.97, 95% CI 0.95–0.99). Categorical-year analyses identified significant non-linearity for HBV, HCV, HIV and any TTI (all p ≤ 0.003), whereas the syphilis pattern was compatible with a linear decline (p = 0.61). Conclusion TTI reactivity among Botswana blood donors remained substantial and temporal patterns differed by pathogen. Syphilis declined consistently, whereas HBV, HCV, HIV and overall TTI reactivity showed non-linear year-to-year variation. Continued screening, confirmatory follow-up, donor counseling and surveillance remain essential to sustain blood safety.

title: Dual Functional Cure in HBV/HIV-1 Co-infection: A Narrative Review for Critical Appraisal of Current Evidence and Conceptual Framework.
abstract: The syndemic of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1) affects millions of people worldwide. Each virus exacerbates the pathogenesis of the other, leading to accelerated liver disease and increased mortality. While combined antiretroviral therapy (cART) suppresses both viruses, it rarely achieves a functional cure, which is defined as sustained hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance for HBV and durable cART-free remission for HIV-1, due to persistent viral reservoirs (covalently closed circular DNA for HBV and integrated proviral DNA for HIV-1). Recent parallel advances in HBV and HIV-1 cure research have generated considerable interest in a "dual functional cure". In this review, we critically evaluate whether current evidence supports such a concept. We first summarize the epidemiology of HBV/HIV-1 coinfection, and then outline coinfection‐specific barriers and opportunities that distinguish a dual cure from a simple superposition of two single‐disease strategies. Next, we compare major cure strategies (interferon‐based, immune checkpoint blockade, Toll‐like receptor agonists, broadly neutralizing antibodies, gene editing, and latency targeting) in terms of evidence level in monoinfection versus coinfection, safety concerns, and translational barriers. Finally, we propose a sequential, personalized framework as a hypothesis‐generating tool, emphasizing that most steps remain extrapolations requiring dedicated coinfection trials. We conclude by defining actionable research priorities, including patient selection criteria, end point choices, and management of hepatitis flares.

analysis.scope_and_question: The syndemic of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1) affects millions of people worldwide. We critically evaluate whether current evidence supports the concept of a "dual functional cure" in HBV/HIV-1 co-infection.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This review is a narrative synthesis of existing evidence on HBV/HIV-1 co-infection. It outlines the epidemiology of the co-infection, compares cure strategies in monoinfection versus coinfection, and evaluates safety concerns and translational barriers. The review does not report a meta-analysis or pooled estimate.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Current evidence suggests that combined antiretroviral therapy (cART) suppresses both HBV and HIV-1 but rarely achieves a functional cure due to persistent viral reservoirs. A dual functional cure, defined as sustained HBsAg seroclearance for HBV and durable cART-free remission for HIV-1, remains a concept under critical appraisal.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that most steps in the proposed sequential, personalized framework for dual functional cure remain extrapolations requiring dedicated coinfection trials. There is a lack of direct evidence on dual functional cure strategies in human co-infection.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Actionable research priorities include defining patient selection criteria, choosing appropriate endpoints, and managing hepatitis flares during treatment. These priorities aim to guide future studies and clinical approaches for dual functional cure in HBV/HIV-1 co-infection.

analysis.summary_en: This review critically evaluates the concept of a dual functional cure in HBV/HIV-1 co-infection. It outlines the epidemiology of the co-infection and discusses the challenges of achieving a functional cure due to persistent viral reservoirs. The review highlights that current evidence is limited and that most proposed strategies remain extrapolations. Research priorities include patient selection, endpoint choices, and managing hepatitis flares. The review emphasizes the need for dedicated coinfection trials to advance the dual functional cure concept.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 和人类免疫缺陷病毒-1 (HIV-1) 的综合症影响着全世界数百万人。我们严格评估当前证据是否支持 HBV/HIV-1 合并感染中的“双重 功能性治愈”概念。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这篇综述是对 HBV/HIV-1 合并感染现有证据的叙述性综合。它概述了混合感染的 流行病学,比较了单一感染与混合感染的治疗策略,并评估了安全问题和转化障碍。该综述未报告荟萃分析或汇总估计。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 目前的证据表明,联合抗逆转录病毒疗法 (cART) 可抑制 HBV 和 HIV-1,但由于病毒 储存宿主 持续存在,很少能达到 功能性治愈。双重 功能性治愈 定义为 HBV 的持续 HBsAg 血清清除和 HIV-1 的持久无 cART 缓解,仍然是一个正在严格评估的概念。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查强调,拟议的双 功能性治愈 连续、个性化框架中的大多数步骤仍然是需要专门的共感染试验的推断。缺乏关于人类双重感染的双重 功能性治愈 策略的直接证据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 可操作的研究重点包括定义患者选择标准、选择适当的终点以及在 治疗 期间管理肝炎发作。这些优先事项旨在指导 HBV/HIV-1 双重感染中双重 功能性治愈 的未来研究和临床方法。

Each virus exacerbates the pathogenesis of the other, leading to accelerated liver disease and increased mortality. While combined antiretroviral therapy (cART) suppresses both viruses, it rarely achieves a functional cure, which is defined as sustained hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance for HBV and durable cART-free remission for HIV-1, due to persistent viral reservoirs (covalently closed circular DNA for HBV and integrated proviral DNA for HIV-1). Recent parallel advances in HBV and HIV-1 cure research have generated considerable interest in a "dual functional cure". In this review, we critically evaluate whether current evidence supports such a concept. We first summarize the epidemiology of HBV/HIV-1 coinfection, and then outline coinfection‐specific barriers and opportunities that distinguish a dual cure from a simple superposition of two single‐disease strategies. Next, we compare major cure strategies (interferon‐based, immune checkpoint blockade, Toll‐like receptor agonists, broadly neutralizing antibodies, gene editing, and latency targeting) in terms of evidence level in monoinfection versus coinfection, safety concerns, and translational barriers. Finally, we propose a sequential, personalized framework as a hypothesis‐generating tool, emphasizing that most steps remain extrapolations requiring dedicated coinfection trials. We conclude by defining actionable research priorities, including patient selection criteria, end point choices, and management of hepatitis flares.
abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 和人类免疫缺陷病毒-1 (HIV-1) 的综合症影响着全世界数百万人。每种病毒都会加剧另一种病毒的 发病机制,导致肝脏疾病加速并增加 死亡率。虽然联合抗逆转录病毒疗法 (cART) 可抑制这两种病毒,但它很少能达到 功能性治愈,功能性治愈 被定义为 HBV 的持续乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 血清清除和 HIV-1 的持久无 cART 缓解,因为持续存在病毒 储存宿主(HBV 的共价闭合环状 DNA 和 HIV-1 的整合原病毒 DNA)。最近 HBV 和 HIV-1 治愈研究的并行进展引起了人们对“双重 功能性治愈”的极大兴趣。在这篇综述中,我们批判性地评估了当前的证据是否支持这一概念。我们首先总结了 HBV/HIV-1 合并感染的 流行病学,然后概述了合并感染特定的障碍和机会,以区分双重治疗和两种单一疾病策略的简单叠加。接下来,我们从单一感染与合并感染的证据水平、安全问题和转化障碍方面比较主要治疗策略(基于干扰素、免疫检查点阻断、Toll 样受体激动剂、广泛中和抗体、基因编辑和潜伏期靶向)。最后,我们提出了一个连续的、个性化的框架作为假设生成工具,强调大多数步骤仍然是需要专门的双重感染试验的推断。最后,我们确定了可行的研究重点,包括患者选择标准、终点选择和肝炎发作的管理。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 和人类免疫缺陷病毒-1 (HIV-1) 的综合症影响着全世界数百万人。我们严格评估当前证据是否支持 HBV/HIV-1 合并感染中的“双重 功能性治愈”概念。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这篇综述是对 HBV/HIV-1 合并感染现有证据的叙述性综合。它概述了混合感染的 流行病学,比较了单一感染与混合感染的治疗策略,并评估了安全问题和转化障碍。该综述未报告荟萃分析或汇总估计。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 目前的证据表明,联合抗逆转录病毒疗法 (cART) 可抑制 HBV 和 HIV-1,但由于病毒 储存宿主 持续存在,很少能达到 功能性治愈。双重 功能性治愈 定义为 HBV 的持续 HBsAg 血清清除和 HIV-1 的持久无 cART 缓解,仍然是一个正在严格评估的概念。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查强调,拟议的双 功能性治愈 连续、个性化框架中的大多数步骤仍然是需要专门的共感染试验的推断。缺乏关于人类双重感染的双重 功能性治愈 策略的直接证据。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 可操作的研究重点包括定义患者选择标准、选择适当的终点以及在 治疗 期间管理肝炎发作。这些优先事项旨在指导 HBV/HIV-1 双重感染中双重 功能性治愈 的未来研究和临床方法。

title: A biologically optimized PEG-IFN-α2 variant exhibits potent anti-HBV and immunomodulatory efficacy.
abstract: Human interferon-alpha (IFN-α) includes 13 subtypes, but only IFN-α2 (a/b) is clinically approved for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) therapy, limited by adverse effects and suboptimal response rates. Previously, we identified IFN-α14 as a superior anti-HBV subtype compared to IFN-α2, leading to the engineering of the IFN-α2-EIFK variant, which mimics IFN-α14's enhanced antiviral activity through targeted mutations at receptor-binding sites. However, the in vivo anti-HBV effects of IFN-α2-EIFK remained unexplored due to its short plasma half-life and lack of immunocompetent murine systems suitable for evaluating human IFN-α activity. Using an immunocompetent IFNAR-hEC mouse model and HBV-infected human-liver chimeric mice etc, we demonstrated that N-terminally PEGylated IFN-α2-EIFK (PEG-IFN-α2-EIFK) suppressed HBV replication and antigen expression approximately 10-fold more effectively than PEG-IFN-α2 at equivalent mass doses, while concurrently activating IFN-γ-like signaling pathways in both hepatocytes and immune cells. Subsequent single-cell analysis of intrahepatic immune cells from IFNAR-hEC mice showed that PEG-IFN-α2-EIFK was associated with enhanced antigen-presenting capacity of macrophages, dendritic cells (DCs), and B cells. In addition, PEG-IFN-α2-EIFK was found to preferentially promote M1-like macrophage polarization, and modulate PD-L1/PD-1 interactions between macrophages and CD8+ T cells, accompanied by attenuation of an exhaustion-associated CD8+ T cell state. In conclusion, this study demonstrates that PEG-IFN-α2-EIFK exhibits greater anti-HBV activity and immunomodulatory potency than PEG-IFN-α2 under equivalent mass dosing, supporting its potential as an enhanced therapeutic candidate for CHB.

title: The Safety and Efficacy of Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir/Voxilaprevir in Patients with Chronic Hepatitis C who Failed Prior Directly Acting Antivirals: A Nationwide Multicenter Study in Taiwan.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Although direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) achieve high cure rates in patients with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, a subset of patients fail first-line DAA therapy. This post-authorization study aimed to evaluate the real-world safety and efficacy of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir (SOF/VEL/VOX) in a DAA-experienced population. METHODS: A total of 116 DAA-experienced patients who received 12 weeks of SOF/VEL/VOX between 2021 and 2024 were enrolled retrospectively and prospectively from 15 sites in Taiwan. The primary objective was to assess safety, including adverse events (AEs), serious adverse events (SAEs), adverse drug reactions (ADRs), serious adverse drug reactions (SADRs), and drug-induced liver injury (DILI); the secondary objective was the sustained virological response (SVR12). RESULTS: Of the 116 patients (Full Analysis Set), the most common prior DAA failures were glecaprevir/pibrentasvir (31.9%) and sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (29.3%). The SVR12 rate was 98.1% (105/107) in the modified full analysis set, with 100% efficacy observed in subgroups with cirrhosis, HBV/HCV coinfection, HIV/HCV coinfection, and those with a history of liver transplantation. Regarding safety, 44.8% of patients experienced at least one AE, although 97.5% of these events were nonserious. The incidence rate of any AE was 2.0 events per person-year (95% confidence interval: 1.5-2.7). The most common AEs included gastrointestinal disorders (28.4%) and infections (12.1%). No cases of DILI, hyperbilirubinemia, SADRs, or treatment-related SAEs occurred. CONCLUSIONS: Twelve weeks of SOF/VEL/VOX is highly effective and well-tolerated as retreatment for chronic hepatitis C after prior DAA failure, with no new safety concerns identified.

title: Patterns of Patient Visits to a Gastroenterology Clinic in a Tertiary Hospital in Sub-Saharan Africa - A Retrospective Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sub-Saharan Africa is experiencing an epidemiological transition where infectious diseases coexist with a rising burden of non-communicable gastrointestinal (GI) disorders. Despite this, detailed data on gastroenterology clinic visit patterns in tertiary centers remain sparse. AIM: To characterize the diagnostic profile, demographic distribution, and monthly/seasonal patterns of patient visits to the specialist gastroenterology clinic of Nnamdi Azikiwe University Teaching Hospital, Nnewi, south east Nigeria. METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted at Nnamdi Azikiwe University Teaching Hospital (NAUTH), Nnewi, Nigeria. Clinical records of 3,128 patients managed between January 2017 and December 2021 were analyzed. Data on demographics, monthly visit distribution, and primary diagnoses were extracted and analyzed using SPSS version 26. RESULTS: The cohort had a mean age of 43.86 ± 15.50 years, with a slight male predominance (51.6%). The most represented age group was 21-40 years (44.7%). Chronic Hepatitis B Virus (CHBV) was the most prevalent diagnosis, accounting for 41.4% of consultations, followed by dyspepsia (13.7%) and decompensated liver cirrhosis (9.2%). Other notable conditions included alcohol-fatty liver disease (AFLD) (3.9%) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) (3.3%). More than half of all consultations (55.6%) occurred during months characterized by high-intensity rainfall (37.6%) and extreme heat waves (18%). CONCLUSION: The findings highlight a "double burden" of disease, where endemic Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) remains the primary public health priority, particularly among the economically active young-adult population, alongside significant rates of functional and lifestyle-related disorders. The high prevalence of advanced cirrhosis suggests late clinical presentation. There is an urgent need for strengthened HBV birth-dose vaccination and expanded local research to develop indigenous, evidence-based management protocols for the region.

title: Gazing Upon the Great Eye: A Rare Presentation of Behcet's Disease.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Behcet's disease is a systemic autoimmune condition presenting classically with recurrent and painful mucocutaneous ulcers. It is more prevalent among Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, and Asian populations. Ocular or neurologic involvement is uncommon, but when present, contributes to significant morbidity and mortality (1). Clinical features are variable and often lead to delays in diagnosis (2). METHOD: We report the case of a 41-year-old female who presented with left-sided pan-uveitis, shifting hypopyon, and retinitis. This followed several months of recurrent oral and genital ulcers, fevers, and constitutional symptoms. Her clinical course was complicated by subacute left lower limb sensory deficits and a new diagnosis of chronic hepatitis B virus infection. Anti-nuclear antibodies and anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies were negative. She was HLA-B*51 positive. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed spinal lesions at the level of T6/T7 involving the right anterior and posterior horns, with possible involvement of the spinothalamic tract. RESULTS: The patient was initially treated with high-dose topical and systemic corticosteroids alongside entecavir, followed by regular infliximab infusions. Her uveitis and mucocutaneous symptoms significantly improved. A three-month progress MRI scan demonstrated radiological improvement with interval reduction in the size of the spinal lesions, though a degree of lower limb symptoms has persisted. CONCLUSION: This case illustrates the high morbidity associated with multi-organ manifestations of Behcet's disease. The heterogenous presentation may lead to diagnostic delays, and clinicians are reminded to consider less typical features of this potentially debilitating condition. A cross-disciplinary approach is particularly valuable and paramount to optimizing care for these patients.

title: Hepatic manifestations of Pica syndrome: multicenter study.
abstract: Pica syndrome, characterized by the persistent ingestion of non-nutritive substances, may be associated with systemic complications, including hepatic involvement. Therefore, we aimed to investigate its hepatic manifestations in a Moroccan cohort. To this end, a prospective multicenter study was conducted from 2021 to 2024 across four healthcare centers, and clinical, biological, imaging, and liver elastography data were collected. Liver fibrosis was assessed using FibroScan® and classified according to METAVIR-equivalent stages. Among 12,520 individuals who consulted, 174 who met the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fourth Edition criteria for Pica syndrome were identified, with a prevalence of 13‰. The median patient age was 46 (range: 37-59) years, with a slight male predominance (sex ratio = 1.18). The most commonly ingested substances were clay (56%), coal (32%), paper (12%), and sand (8%). The main symptoms were abdominal discomfort (68%) and asthenia (24%). Sideropenic anemia was present in 64% of patients, and ferritin levels were low in 72%. The median liver stiffness was 5.7 (range: 4.3-8.1) kPa. Fibrosis staging showed stages F0-F1, F2, F3, and F4 in 68.4%, 14.4%, 1.7%, and 15.5% of the patients. Chronic hepatitis B virus infection was the most frequent associated etiology (47.7%). Fibrosis severity was significantly associated with liver disease etiology (p < 0.001) but not with sex or anthropometric parameters. Multivariable analysis showed that hepatitis B virus infection was independently associated with lower odds of advanced fibrosis (odds ratio = 0.16, 95% confidence interval: 0.04-0.61; p = 0.008). Pica syndrome showed heterogeneous hepatic manifestations, while liver fibrosis severity appeared to be mainly related to the underlying liver disease etiology.

title: UNIVERSAL INFECTIOUS DISEASE SCREENING AND CATCH UP VACCINATION IN UNACCOMPANIED CHILDREN AND YOUNG PEOPLE SEEKING ASYLUM AND REFUGEES(CYPSAR-U): A RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT
abstract: Background: Children and Young People Seeking Asylum and Refugees who are unaccompanied (CYPSAR-U) are a growing population in the UK with complex healthcare needs. Universal screening demonstrates significant rates of infectious disease, many of which are asymptomatic but readily treatable when identified, supporting its importance. Vaccination histories are frequently incomplete or unavailable making timely catch-up immunisation essential. However, there is limited evidence describing vaccination uptake following specialist assessment. This audit evaluated infectious disease screening outcomes and catch-up vaccination uptake among CYPSAR-U attending a paediatric infectious disease service, compared with Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health (RCPCH) guidelines. title: Love, Sex, and Immunosuppression: A Sexual Health Overview for the Transplant Clinician.
abstract: Abstract Sexual health is a critical, yet often overlooked, aspect of comprehensive care for solid organ transplant recipients. While transplantation can restore overall health and quality of life, patients may continue to experience sexual dysfunction because of physiological, psychological, and pharmacological factors. Furthermore, transplant recipients remain at risk for sexually transmitted infections (STIs), including HIV, human papillomavirus (HPV), syphilis, and others, with implications for both patient and graft outcomes. HPV-associated malignancies, particularly anal squamous cell carcinoma, occur at significantly higher rates in this population, highlighting the need for recommendations on targeted screening and vaccination. This review addresses the spectrum of sexual health issues across transplant populations-including liver, kidney, heart, and lung recipients-with practical guidance on sexual function, STI screening, and risk reduction strategies. We outline current evidence and recommendations for preexposure and postexposure prophylaxis against HIV and bacterial STIs, including the use of tenofovir-based preexposure prophylaxis and doxycycline postexposure prophylaxis. We also aim to highlight the role of immunization against HPV, hepatitis B, hepatitis A, and monkeypox virus, emphasizing safety, timing, and efficacy considerations in immunocompromised individuals. Despite growing awareness, implementation of routine sexual health assessment and STI prevention strategies remains inconsistent in transplant medicine. We call for greater integration of sexual health into transplant care pathways and identify key research priorities to optimize outcomes. Clinicians should feel empowered to initiate open conversations, advocate for vaccination and prophylaxis, and tailor care based on individualized risk. This comprehensive update offers practical tools and recommendations to improve sexual health in solid organ transplant recipients.

title: Increased Hepatitis D Testing in Canada Identifies More HDV-Positive Individuals: A Multi-Provincial Analysis, 2022-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: CASL/AMMI 2025 guidelines recommend reflex anti-HDV testing for all hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive individuals, replacing risk-based screening, yet Canadian data on HDV testing and detection remain limited. In Canada, only Quebec offers anti-HDV testing; other regions refer samples to the National Microbiology Laboratory (NML), where HDV RNA confirmation is centralised. We assessed HDV testing volume, seroprevalence, RNA positivity, and genotypes in referred samples and randomly selected archived HBsAg-positive samples. METHODS: Anti-HDV results from Quebec and the NML from August 2022 to July 2024 were analysed and compared with a 2012-2019 national survey. To complement referral-based surveillance, 3386 randomly selected archived HBsAg-positive samples from five provinces were tested. Seropositive samples underwent HDV RNA testing and genotyping at NML. RESULTS: Among 8401 unique referred samples, 271 (3.2%; 95% CI, 2.9-3.6) were anti-HDV positive, of which 117 (43.2%; 95% CI, 37.4-49.1) were HDV RNA positive. Compared with 2012-2019, annual testing volume increased fourfold (1011 to 4201 tests/year), while annual detection increased from 48 to 136 anti-HDV-positive individuals and from 31 to 59 HDV RNA-positive individuals. Among archived samples, 67/3386 (2.0%; 95% CI, 1.6-2.5) were anti-HDV positive, and 14/67 (20.9%; 95% CI, 12.9-32.1) were RNA positive. Genotypes 1, 2, 5, 7, and 8 were detected. CONCLUSIONS: Increased HDV testing in Canada was associated with greater detection of anti-HDV-positive and HDV RNA-positive individuals despite lower positivity rates. HDV RNA detection and multiple genotypes in archived HBsAg-positive samples support universal reflex anti-HDV testing, with RNA confirmation, harmonised reporting, and integrated HBV/HDV surveillance.

title: CATCHUP VACCINATION PROGRAMS IN THE STATE OF QATAR: CLOSING IMMUNITY GAPS THROUGH STRATEGIC PLANNING AND IMPLEMENTATION
abstract: Background: Vaccination helps the body develop immunity to infections, protecting individuals when exposed to harmful microorganisms. It provides long-term, cost-effective protection without causing illness, usually with only mild reactions. In addition to protecting vaccinated individuals, immunization also helps protect the wider community through herd immunity, reducing the spread of disease to those who are not vaccinated. A Qatar-based catch-up immunization program addresses vaccination gaps among defaulters and underimmunized populations. The guideline aims to support implementation of the National Vaccination Programme by providing clear immunization guidance and ensuring safe, standardized vaccination practices across departments for diverse patient groups. Method: The Health Protection & CDC Department of the Ministry of Public Health(MOPH), in line with the expanded immunization program, developed an advanced and modern child immunization program . The National Vaccination Committee is also constantly reviewing and making adjustments to the vaccination schedule in accordance with the trends of disease prevention in the country. Currently, (Qatar’s National Immunization Guidelines for Vaccine Providers) there are twelve vaccines used in the national program for basic vaccinations in the State of Qatar, providing children with immunity against fourteen diseases. Result: Full compliance with neonatal vaccination standards was achieved during the study period. All well newborns (100%) received Bacillus Calmette–Guérin (BCG) and Hepatitis B vaccinations within the first 24 hours of birth. Overall vaccination practices demonstrated (100%) adherence to the national immunization schedule in accordance with MOPH guidelines, reflecting effective implementation of standardized newborn vaccination processes. Conclusion: A structured, guideline-based approach to catch-up vaccination effectively addresses gaps in non-immunized populations, improving overall immunization coverage and ensuring alignment with national standards across services.

title: Use of N-of-1 trials in liver diseases: A systematic review
abstract: BACKGROUND Chronic liver diseases are heterogeneous and include autoimmune, genetic, metabolic, cholestatic, vascular, and idiopathic etiologies. Rare or slowly progressive conditions may make conventional randomized controlled trials difficult to conduct. The N-of-1 trial design offers a rigorous alternative for evaluating individualized treatment effects. AIM To map the extent, nature, and characteristics of N-of-1 trials in liver diseases and identify research gaps. METHODS We followed the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology for scoping reviews and PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews reporting standards, using the Population, Concept, and Context framework. The Population comprised patients with chronic liver disease, the Concept was the use of an N-of-1 trial design, and the Context included clinical or health care settings worldwide, without geographic restriction. We searched MEDLINE (via Ovid), EMBASE, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from inception through March 17, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records in Covidence, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Eligible sources were English-language publications explicitly using an N-of-1 design in patients with liver diseases. Data charting captured study design, population, interventions, outcomes, and statistical methods. According to Joanna Briggs Institute guidance, a formal risk-of-bias assessment was not required; however, an optional narrative appraisal was performed. RESULTS Of 76 records identified, 2 empirical N-of-1 studies met the eligibility criteria. One evaluated oral thiamine in 3 patients with chronic hepatitis B and reported reduced aminotransferase levels and improved virological markers using t -tests. However, the pooled analysis of data from only 3 patients was statistically problematic and should not be considered strong evidence. The second study evaluated ursodeoxycholic acid in a patient with hepatic sarcoidosis over four crossover cycles and demonstrated improvement in cholestasis using a Wilcoxon test for paired data. The optional narrative appraisal found that both studies lacked randomization and blinding and did not use pre-specified protocols, raising concerns about internal validity. CONCLUSION No identified study used aggregated N-of-1 analyses, Bayesian methods, or frameworks for integrating N-of-1 evidence into clinical decision-making. N-of-1 trials remain markedly underused in hepatology despite the presence of rare, stable, chronic liver diseases for which traditional randomized controlled trials may be impractical. Broader adoption, supported by Bayesian analytical methods, electronic health record integration, and reporting aligned with the CONSORT extension specifically developed for N-of-1 trials, could advance personalized care and complement conventional trial designs in future hepatology research.

title: Phytochemicals and Antimicrobial Applications of Aloe vera and Urtica dioica: A Scoping Review and Scientometric Analysis
abstract: Background/Objectives: In the context of antimicrobial resistance, this study mapped the evidence on phytochemicals, extracts, fractions and formulations of Aloe vera, as the primary species, and Urtica dioica, as a comparative case, with antibacterial, antifungal and antiviral activity and identified research trends and gaps. Methods: We conducted a scoping review following PRISMA-ScR, integrated with a scientometric analysis. Of 1359 records retrieved from Scopus (5 October 2026), we included 477 documents published in 2010–2026 (409 primary studies) after screening. We coded chemical, technological, microbiological and quality variables using lexical rules validated against manual coding and analysed production and impact indicators together with co-authorship, co-occurrence and co-citation networks. Results: Output grew at a compound annual rate of 15.5% and was concentrated on A. vera (88.9%) and on in vitro studies (61.6%). Only 27.4% of primary studies named a specific phytochemical; aloe-emodin (C15H10O5) was the most studied compound; its experimental antiviral evidence concerns influenza A and hepatitis B viruses, whereas evidence against SARS-CoV-2 is computational only. In abstracts, separation or structure-based analytical techniques appeared in 5.4% of studies, 1.7% reported standardised extracts, and 2.9% tested methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. In 40.3% of primary studies, the plant material was combined with other active components. Between 2010–2015 and 2021–2026, nanomaterials rose from 1.8% to 30.5% of studies, whereas studies with human participants remained scarce (5.9%; 3.7% randomised). Conclusions: The evidence is abundant but preliminary and poorly characterised chemically. Pharmaceutical development of both species requires standardised extracts with quantified markers, safety assessment, testing against resistant pathogens and randomised clinical trials.

Of 1359 records retrieved from Scopus (5 October 2026), we included 477 documents published in 2010–2026 (409 primary studies) after screening. We coded chemical, technological, microbiological and quality variables using lexical rules validated against manual coding and analysed production and impact indicators together with co-authorship, co-occurrence and co-citation networks. Results: Output grew at a compound annual rate of 15.5% and was concentrated on A. vera (88.9%) and on in vitro studies (61.6%). Only 27.4% of primary studies named a specific phytochemical; aloe-emodin (C15H10O5) was the most studied compound; its experimental antiviral evidence concerns influenza A and hepatitis B viruses, whereas evidence against SARS-CoV-2 is computational only. In abstracts, separation or structure-based analytical techniques appeared in 5.4% of studies, 1.7% reported standardised extracts, and 2.9% tested methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. In 40.3% of primary studies, the plant material was combined with other active components. Between 2010–2015 and 2021–2026, nanomaterials rose from 1.8% to 30.5% of studies, whereas studies with human participants remained scarce (5.9%; 3.7% randomised). Conclusions: The evidence is abundant but preliminary and poorly characterised chemically. Pharmaceutical development of both species requires standardised extracts with quantified markers, safety assessment, testing against resistant pathogens and randomised clinical trials.

title: Trajectories of immune reconstitution and the risk factors of immunological non-responsiveness following ART in people with HIV and HBV or HCV-coinfection
abstract: Background Although antiretroviral therapy (ART) is now widely used, long-term immune reconstitution in different populations of HIV remains suboptimal. Co-infected participants were stratified into HIV/HBV and HIV/HCV-coinfection groups to compare CD4 + T-cell recovery trajectories and related factors. Methods This study employed a retrospective cohort design, drawing on records from the AIDS Comprehensive Response Information Management System (CRIMS) in Hunan Province, China. A total of 16,231 PLHIV were followed up from 2016 to 2023, including 1,863 individuals with HBV/HCV-coinfection. These co-infected participants were stratified into HIV/HBV and HIV/HCV coinfection groups to compare their CD4 + T-cell recovery trajectories. The generalized additive model (GAM) was used to fit the longitudinal recovery trajectory of CD4 + T-cells, and the Markov Chain Monte Carlo generalized linear mixed models (MCMCglm) estimated the posterior mean of coefficients of complete immune recovery (CIR). Multivariate logistic regression (LR) was utilized to determine independent risk factors associated with INR. Results GAM indicated that the HIV mono-infection (2.85, 95%CI: 2.72~3.01) achieved CD4 + T-cell counts >500 cells/μL significantly faster than the HIV/HBV (3.95 years, 95%CI: 2.95~5.13) and HIV/HCV-coinfection (3.91 years, 95%CI: 3.02~5.29). Regarding CIR, MCMCglm showed that females were associated with an increased CIR probability in HIV/HCV-coinfection. Advanced age, heterosexual transmission, advanced WHO clinical stages, and lower baseline CD4 + T-cell counts were associated with reduced CIR probability in both co-infections. Conversely, regarding INR, LR identified advanced age, heterosexual transmission, low baseline CD4 + T-cell counts, and advanced WHO clinical stages as significant risk factors shared by both co-infections. Conclusions HIV/HBV and HIV/HCV-coinfection significantly delay long-term immune reconstitution compared to HIV mono-infection. Advanced age, heterosexual transmission, low baseline CD4 + T-cell counts, and advanced WHO clinical stages predict poor sustained immune recovery in both co-infections. These findings underscore the necessity for longitudinal monitoring and tailored management to optimize durable immune outcomes in high-risk HIV patients.

Co-infected participants were stratified into HIV/HBV and HIV/HCV-coinfection groups to compare CD4 + T-cell recovery trajectories and related factors. Methods This study employed a retrospective cohort design, drawing on records from the AIDS Comprehensive Response Information Management System (CRIMS) in Hunan Province, China. A total of 16,231 PLHIV were followed up from 2016 to 2023, including 1,863 individuals with HBV/HCV-coinfection. These co-infected participants were stratified into HIV/HBV and HIV/HCV coinfection groups to compare their CD4 + T-cell recovery trajectories. The generalized additive model (GAM) was used to fit the longitudinal recovery trajectory of CD4 + T-cells, and the Markov Chain Monte Carlo generalized linear mixed models (MCMCglm) estimated the posterior mean of coefficients of complete immune recovery (CIR). Multivariate logistic regression (LR) was utilized to determine independent risk factors associated with INR. Results GAM indicated that the HIV mono-infection (2.85, 95%CI: 2.72~3.01) achieved CD4 + T-cell counts >500 cells/μL significantly faster than the HIV/HBV (3.95 years, 95%CI: 2.95~5.13) and HIV/HCV-coinfection (3.91 years, 95%CI: 3.02~5.29). Regarding CIR, MCMCglm showed that females were associated with an increased CIR probability in HIV/HCV-coinfection. Advanced age, heterosexual transmission, advanced WHO clinical stages, and lower baseline CD4 + T-cell counts were associated with reduced CIR probability in both co-infections. Conversely, regarding INR, LR identified advanced age, heterosexual transmission, low baseline CD4 + T-cell counts, and advanced WHO clinical stages as significant risk factors shared by both co-infections. Conclusions HIV/HBV and HIV/HCV-coinfection significantly delay long-term immune reconstitution compared to HIV mono-infection. Advanced age, heterosexual transmission, low baseline CD4 + T-cell counts, and advanced WHO clinical stages predict poor sustained immune recovery in both co-infections. These findings underscore the necessity for longitudinal monitoring and tailored management to optimize durable immune outcomes in high-risk HIV patients.

title: NEWBORN OUTCOMES OF BABIES BORN UNDER A FAITH-BASED, MULTI-AGENCY MATERNAL AND CHILD HEALTH PROGRAMME IN SINGAPORE
abstract: Background and Aims: Strong evidence has underscored the importance of upstream interventions to improve maternal and child health (MCH). A needs analysis of Singaporean Malay/Muslim women found significant gaps in MCH outcomes, with faith highlighted as a possible determinant of health compliance. Project-Achieving-Resilient-and-Inspiring Families (Project ARIF) was a pilot faith-based community programme to improve MCH among Malay/Muslims in Singapore, starting at marriage. We enrolled pregnant women who were part of Project ARIF and followed them longitudinally through their pregnancies and early parenthood journeys. We present the newborn outcomes of babies born to mothers who participated in this research study. Methods: In Singapore, Muslim marriage solemnisers journey with their newlywed couples for the first few years of marriage to provide spiritual guidance. Doctors, nurses and social workers from KK-Women’s-and-Children’s-Hospital (KKH) leveraged on this by upskilling solemnisers with basic MCH knowledge to guide newlyweds more holistically in their early family journeys. Couples who had higher needs were referred for multi-disciplinary interventions conducted in mosques and community spaces by Project ARIF's medical team. Pregnant women were enrolled into a longitudinal study from 2022-2026. They were supported with pregnancy, lactation and postnatal counselling. They were asked to report on the outcomes of their babies at birth. Results: 151 pregnant women were enrolled, with 87 babies born to date (Figure 1). Mothers did not report any significant antenatal complications. The mean gestational age at birth was 38+5 weeks (Standard Deviation [SD] 1+1 week), with the lowest at 35+6 weeks. The mean birth weight was 3037.2g (SD 392.8g). 92.0% of babies had normal birth weights for gestational age, and 95.4% received both nationally recommended birth vaccines - BCG and Hepatitis B. Only one baby had an eventful birth requiring admission to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit for initial breathing difficulty. 97.7% of mothers initiated breastfeeding at birth, compared to prevalence of 49-65% reported in Singapore's National Breastfeeding and Child Feeding Survey 2021/22 . All babies were discharged well with no chronic medical diagnoses. Conclusion: Our study is the first in South-East Asia to assess a novel model-of-care; the integration of medical, social and religious support at the point of marriage to improve downstream MCH outcomes. None of the mothers in this study had antenatal complications or significantly premature births. The majority of babies born in this cohort to date had good birth outcomes, including much higher prevalence of early breastfeeding initiation, compared to national data. These preliminary findings of newborn babies born to mothers under Project ARIF are very promising, and suggest that combining faith and culture in health messaging can make a difference in MCH literacy and compliance. Strong collaborations with faith leaders and influential community figures are important avenues to improve MCH and overall population health.

title: Robust parameter estimation and dose-fractionation for ptychographic single-particle analysis at near-atomic resolution
abstract: We present a complete workflow for the determination of biomolecular structures by single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy using ptychography. To account for the prominent dose damage in biological specimens dose-fractionated data acquisition and processing are introduced. Automated preprocessing techniques estimate the probe shape and scanning geometry before the ptychographic reconstruction by utilising the shadow image inside the Ronchigram. Standard ptychographic single-particle analysis is performed using tobacco mosaic virus, apoferritin and hepatitis B virus capsids. We finally give a demonstration of dose-fractionated ptychography utilising multiple scans of the same area at low dose reaching near-atomic resolution (3.3 Å), allowing for the automated building of atomic models.

title: CRISPR/Cas12a-Triggered Dual-Mode Electrochemical and Raman-Silent Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Biosensing for Sensitive HBV DNA Detection.
abstract: Sensitive and reliable quantification of hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA is important for monitoring viral replication and therapeutic response. Electrochemical (EC) sensing offers simple quantitative readout, but resolving current changes at low target concentrations remains challenging. Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS), in contrast, provides signal amplification but generally requires specialized optical instrumentation and may suffer from matrix interference. title: Clinical Significance of Indeterminate Antibody to Hepatitis C in Cancer Patients.
abstract: Most patients with cancer are screened for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection using an antibody to HCV (anti-HCV) test. However, the importance of an indeterminate anti-HCV result is unknown. We investigated the clinical significance of an indeterminate anti-HCV result in cancer patients. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of cancer patients screened for HCV infection using ARCHITECT Anti-HCV at our institution between October 2016 and July 2024. Patients were categorized based on their anti-HCV results as patients with indeterminate anti-HCV and undetectable HCV-RNA in the absence of HCV treatment, and patients with reactive anti-HCV and chronic infection. We compared the two groups using univariable analyses and multivariable logistic regression analysis. Of the 112,180 patients screened with anti-HCV, 114 (0.1%) had indeterminate results; 101 of them with confirmed cancer were further analysed. Anti-HCV testing was repeated in 24 (24%) patients; most (84%) had non-reactive (46%) or indeterminate (38%) results. Among the 101 patients with indeterminate anti-HCV, 98 (97%) did not have proven HCV infection, but 3 (3%) had HCV infection. Multivariable analysis showed that male sex (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.22, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.40-3.53, p < 0.001), age ≥ 60 years (aOR 1.61, 95% CI 1.01-2.56, p = 0.046), hepatitis B or HIV coinfection (aOR 3.13, 95% CI 1.21-8.11, p = 0.019) and cirrhosis (aOR 6.67, 95% CI 2.05-21.69, p = 0.002) were more likely to have chronic than an indeterminate anti-HCV result. Indeterminate anti-HCV results are uncommon in cancer patients and rarely indicate HCV infection.

title: Immune checkpoint modulation beyond cancer: a conceptual framework for small-molecule host-directed antiviral therapy
abstract: Immune checkpoints are important regulators of antiviral immunity, but their roles in viral infections are more complex than the conventional model of immune inhibition. Although sustained checkpoint signaling can impair antiviral T-cell function and contribute to viral persistence, it can also limit immune-mediated tissue damage. This dual role presents a major challenge for therapeutic intervention, as indiscriminate checkpoint inhibition may improve viral control at the expense of increased immunopathology. In this review, we examine how viral infections reshape immune checkpoint networks through antiviral signaling, protein homeostasis, cellular metabolism, and tissue-specific immune regulation. We discuss the implications of these mechanisms for chronic viral infections, including human immunodeficiency virus and hepatitis B and C viruses, as well as acute respiratory infections caused by influenza A virus, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, and respiratory syncytial virus. Particular attention is given to small-molecule checkpoint modulators and their potential to regulate protein interactions, stability, localization, and signaling beyond conventional receptor–ligand blockade. We distinguish the pharmacological evidence supporting these compounds, which is derived primarily from oncology-related research, from the much more limited evidence of their direct antiviral activity. However, direct evidence that these compounds can achieve effective checkpoint modulation while improving viral control and limiting tissue injury remains limited. We therefore discuss the need for rigorous target validation and a more precise approach to patient selection and treatment design. Integrating viral burden, antiviral T-cell function, checkpoint activity, and inflammatory status may help identify patients most likely to benefit from intervention and guide treatment timing, intensity, and discontinuation. Combining checkpoint modulation with direct-acting antivirals or other host-directed therapies may offer additional benefits if viral suppression and immune restoration can be appropriately balanced. A shift from sustained checkpoint blockade toward context-dependent immune modulation may provide a basis for developing more precise host-directed antiviral strategies.

title: Open Salvage Microwave Ablation for Refractory Diffuse Hepatic Oozing After Abandonment of Planned Hepatectomy for Large Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: We report a 50-year-old man with hepatitis B-related compensated Child-Pugh A cirrhosis, an 8.9-cm primary hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and a suspected 1.7-cm satellite nodule, who was initially planned for hepatectomy. During hepatic mobilisation, persistent diffuse surface parenchymal oozing developed. Despite conventional topical haemostatic measures and a 12-minute Pringle manoeuvre, severe oozing (estimated blood loss approximately 2000 mL) was only partially controlled. Given the pre-existing portal hypertension, continued resection carried a high risk of post-hepatectomy liver failure, and hepatectomy was therefore abandoned. Rather than simple haemostasis and abdominal closure without tumour-directed therapy, open intraoperative ultrasound-guided microwave ablation (open IOUS-MWA) was performed to achieve dual objectives: local oncological control and consolidation of haemostasis. Importantly, this scenario is distinct from previously reported MWA for discrete tumour-related bleeding, in which ablation is used primarily for haemostasis. Three-month follow-up contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (CE-MRI) identified residual disease despite post-operatively initiated concurrent targeted-immunotherapy, necessitating supplementary percutaneous MWA. No extrahepatic metastasis was detected during follow-up; however, durable local tumour control could not be confirmed, and the oncological benefit cannot be attributed exclusively to this salvage ablation. Larger cohorts with prolonged follow-up are needed to validate this approach.

title: HBV-induced modulations in DC subsets reprogram NK cell responses
abstract: Abstract Background Infection with hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a significant global health concern, often progressing to chronic infection in individuals unable to mount an effective immune response. Natural Killer (NK) cells and Dendritic cells (DC) are a prominent arm of innate immunity and defence against viral infections, but their functions are compromised in HBV patients. The mechanisms through which HBV disrupts the DC-NK cell interactions remain unclear. Methods We investigated how human HBV influences the interplay between cDC1, cDC2 and pDC subpopulations and NK cells. Blood-derived DC subsets were exposed to HBV, then co-cultured with NK cells under different stimulation conditions. NK cell phenotype, function and secreted factors were analysed. In parallel, serum from patients with acute and chronic HBV, as well as healthy donors, was assessed for immune mediators. Results HBV-exposed DCs altered NK cell phenotype without affecting degranulation, and significantly changed cytokine and soluble immune checkpoint secretion in a subset-specific manner. In TLR3-stimulated cDC1/NK cocultures, HBV pre-exposure of cDC1 increased MCP-1, MIP-1α, MIG, and IP-10 secretion while reducing the release of sCTLA-4, sLAG-3, and sGITR. Similarly, HBV pre-exposure of cDC2 enhanced MCP-1, MIP-1α, and MIP-1β production in TLR8-stimulated cDC2/NK cocultures. In contrast, HBV-conditioned pDCs reduced NK cell secretion of IFN-γ, sCTLA-4, sLAG-3, and sGITR. Serum analysis demonstrated a systemic increase in cytokine levels during acute HBV infection, with MIG and IP-10 levels showing a positive correlation with viral load. Conclusions These findings reveal novel mechanisms by which HBV modulates DC–NK cell communication.

title: Global Dynamics of a Diffusive HBV/HTLV-1 Coinfection Model
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human T-cell lymphotropic virus type 1 (HTLV-1) are persistent pathogens that pose major global public-health challenges. However, their interplay remains poorly understood, and mathematical studies addressing their concurrent dynamics are scarce. In this paper, we examine a partial differential equation (PDE) model of HBV/HTLV-1 co-infection, accounting for the spatial mobility of viruses and cells. We also model the mitotic division of cells that are actively infected. We first prove that the system is well posed. We then determine the equilibria of the model and the threshold parameters that govern their existence, and establish their global asymptotic stability using suitable Lyapunov functions. The analytical results are confirmed by numerical simulations. We also study how sensitive R1 (HTLV-1 single-infection) and R2 (HBV single-infection) and the co-infection thresholds R3 and R4 are to each parameter, to find out which parameters have the most influence on the outcome of co-infection. Furthermore, the effects of CD4+ T-cell activation (σ) and mitotic proliferation (μ*) on the co-infection equilibrium (EP3) are examined, alongside a comparative assessment of single- and co-infection scenarios. The findings provide a theoretical framework to shed light on within-host pathogenesis of HBV/HTLV-1 co-infection and offer valuable insights for the development of targeted therapeutic and preventive strategies.

source_records.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human T-cell lymphotropic virus type 1 (HTLV-1) are persistent pathogens that pose major global public-health challenges. However, their interplay remains poorly understood, and mathematical studies addressing their concurrent dynamics are scarce. In this paper, we examine a partial differential equation (PDE) model of HBV/HTLV-1 co-infection, accounting for the spatial mobility of viruses and cells. We also model the mitotic division of cells that are actively infected. We first prove that the system is well posed. We then determine the equilibria of the model and the threshold parameters that govern their existence, and establish their global asymptotic stability using suitable Lyapunov functions. The analytical results are confirmed by numerical simulations. We also study how sensitive R1 (HTLV-1 single-infection) and R2 (HBV single-infection) and the co-infection thresholds R3 and R4 are to each parameter, to find out which parameters have the most influence on the outcome of co-infection. Furthermore, the effects of CD4+ T-cell activation (σ) and mitotic proliferation (μ*) on the co-infection equilibrium (EP3) are examined, alongside a comparative assessment of single- and co-infection scenarios. The findings provide a theoretical framework to shed light on within-host pathogenesis of HBV/HTLV-1 co-infection and offer valuable insights for the development of targeted therapeutic and preventive strategies.

title: Overview of Health Status among Roma Population in Romania: A Scoping Review
abstract: Background: Roma are widely recognized as Europe ‘s largest ethnic minority and in-dependent estimates suggest that up to two million people live in Romania. Despite well-documented socioeconomic disadvantage, no prior review has synthesized evi-dence on the health status of Roma in Romania. Objectives: This scoping review mapped the literature on healthcare access, quality of life, chronic disease burden and communicable disease exposure among Roma communities in Romania. Methods: Us-ing the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we con-ducted a systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Science Direct and supplemented by grey literature and reference-list screening, for studies published 2010–2025 in English or Romanian. Results: Thirty-nine sources (35 studies and 4 in-stitutional reports) met the inclusion criteria. Roma communities experience a life-expectancy gap of 3.5–4.6 years, markedly lower preventive-care uptake (39% vs 71% in the general population), and high rates of being uninsured (42–59%). Chronic disease burden was substantially higher than in the general population: hypertension prevalence ranged 33–67%, type 2 diabetes from 10–29%, and obesity from 32–62%, with evidence of earlier onset and more severe complications, including higher pro-gression to chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease. Health-related quality of life and mental health indicators were uniformly worse among Roma. Evidence on communicable diseases was sparse but suggested elevated hepatitis B/C prevalence and greater severity of measles and COVID-19. Conclusions: Roma communities in Romania experience markedly poorer health outcomes across nearly all domains ex-amined, driven by intersecting socioeconomic, structural and behavioral determinants.

title: CAUSAS DE INAPTIDÃO EM SERVIÇOS HEMOTERÁPICOS DO ESTADO DE SÃO PAULO: UMA ANÁLISE SOBRE SEGURANÇA, EFICIÊNCIA E ATENDIMENTO HUMANIZADO
abstract: Blood donation is essential to healthcare services, and donor screening aims to protect donors and recipients. This study analyzed factors associated with blood donor deferral in hemotherapy services in the State of São Paulo, considering transfusion safety, service efficiency, and humanized care. This observational, qualitative-quantitative study was characterized as a case report and complemented by a literature and documentary review. Data were collected through an electronic questionnaire directed at hemotherapy professionals. Among reported temporary deferrals, 75% were related to medication use and 25% to recent vaccination. Among permanent deferral causes, hepatitis B or C and heart disease each accounted for 50%, while hematological diseases, kidney diseases, diabetes, and use of drugs or illicit substances each accounted for 25%. Participants could select up to three permanent causes; therefore, percentages are not mutually exclusive. The findings highlight the importance of careful screening and humanized communication to integrate safety and efficiency.

title: Diagnostic and prognostic value of CHI3L1 combined with AFP, AFP-L3%, DCP, and GP73 in chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Background Conventional serological biomarkers show unsatisfactory diagnostic performance for chronic liver disease and associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic value of serum chitinase-3-like protein 1 (CHI3L1), either alone or combined with traditional biomarkers, in liver diseases. Methods A total of 270 subjects were enrolled, including 47 healthy controls, 47 chronic hepatitis B, 47 liver cirrhosis, 82 HCC, and 47 postoperative HCC patients. Serum levels of CHI3L1, AFP, AFP-L3%, DCP, and GP73 were quantified. ROC curves, subgroup analyses based on BCLC stage, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression were performed. Results Serum CHI3L1 levels rose progressively from chronic hepatitis B and liver cirrhosis to HCC (P<0.001), positively correlating with liver disease severity. The AUC values of CHI3L1 for diagnosing chronic hepatitis B and liver cirrhosis were 0.783 and 0.818, respectively, Using non-malignant chronic liver disease as controls to reflect real-world high-risk surveillance, the AUC of CHI3L1 for HCC diagnosis was 0.904, which increased to 0.939 after combined detection with four conventional biomarkers. Notably, in early-stage HCC (BCLC 0/A), CHI3L1 exhibited superior sensitivity (94.44%) compared to AFP (61.11%). Multivariable Cox regression analysis confirmed that elevated CHI3L1 (HR = 9.281, 95% CI: 2.738-31.455, P<0.001) was an independent risk factor, while surgical resection (HR = 0.111, P<0.001) was a protective factor for mortality in HCC patients. Conclusion Serum CHI3L1 has moderate diagnostic value for chronic hepatitis B and liver cirrhosis and excellent diagnostic efficacy for HCC. Combined detection of CHI3L1 with four conventional biomarkers can significantly improve the diagnostic accuracy of HCC. As an independent prognostic risk factor for HCC, CHI3L1 is a promising auxiliary indicator for HCC screening and postoperative risk stratification.

title: Breaking the Paradigm: A Case of Fatal Adenovirus Hepatitis Without Known Immunosuppression
abstract: Acute liver failure (ALF) can result from a variety of causes and follows a highly variable disease course, which makes both its diagnosis and treatment challenging. Common causes of acute liver failure include viral hepatitis (particularly hepatitis B and C), drug-induced liver injury (such as acetaminophen toxicity), alcohol-related liver damage, autoimmune hepatitis, and ischemic hepatitis due to shock or hypoperfusion. In some cases, the cause may remain unknown. In those who have ALF in the United States, the majority of patients experience spontaneous survival, while others undergo liver transplantation or die without transplantation. Our presumed immunocompetent patient initially presented from outside the facility with non-specific symptoms and was subsequently transferred to a liver transplant center because of markedly abnormal liver enzymes concerning for acute liver failure. Upon arrival at our facility, the patient's clinical course progressed rapidly before a complete diagnostic evaluation could be performed. The cause of death was likely multifactorial, with postmortem biopsy identifying adenovirus hepatitis as a potential contributing etiology among other factors.

Common causes of acute liver failure include viral hepatitis (particularly hepatitis B and C), drug-induced liver injury (such as acetaminophen toxicity), alcohol-related liver damage, autoimmune hepatitis, and ischemic hepatitis due to shock or hypoperfusion. In some cases, the cause may remain unknown. In those who have ALF in the United States, the majority of patients experience spontaneous survival, while others undergo liver transplantation or die without transplantation. Our presumed immunocompetent patient initially presented from outside the facility with non-specific symptoms and was subsequently transferred to a liver transplant center because of markedly abnormal liver enzymes concerning for acute liver failure. Upon arrival at our facility, the patient's clinical course progressed rapidly before a complete diagnostic evaluation could be performed. The cause of death was likely multifactorial, with postmortem biopsy identifying adenovirus hepatitis as a potential contributing etiology among other factors.

title: The Nucleoside Analogue NITD008, Alone or Combined With Ribavirin, Potently Reduces Hepatitis E Virus Infection in Humanised Mice.
abstract: Background and aims Hepatitis E virus (HEV) infection is becoming increasingly clinically relevant worldwide, but no approved antiviral therapy currently exists. Ribavirin (RBV) is used off-label for immunosuppressed patients with chronic hepatitis E, although it is effective in only 80% of patients and linked to side effects. The nucleoside analogue NITD008 was shown to be effective against a broad range of RNA viruses. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy of NITD008, alone or in combination with RBV, in humanised mice stably infected with HEV. Methods Mice received either NITD008 alone (20 mg/Kg/day) by oral gavage for up to 2 weeks, or 5 mg/Kg NITD008 alone or in combination with RBV (50 mg/Kg). Viral changes were determined in faeces, blood and intrahepatically. Results NITD008 efficiently reduced HEV loads to undetectable levels in serum and by > 4log 10 in faeces within 1 week. Intrahepatic analysis showed a ∆log 10 : 2.5 reduction in HEV RNA levels in treated mice compared to controls after 2 weeks. Imaging showed fewer HEV-RNA-positive human hepatocytes in treated mice. NITD008 did not increase serum markers of hepatocyte death. Combination therapy induced stronger suppression of HEV RNA in faeces (∆log 10 : 5.02) than RBV monotherapy (∆log 10 : 1.08), despite lower NITD008 doses. Conclusions This study demonstrates the non-toxicity of NITD008 towards human hepatocytes and more potent antiviral activity compared to RBV in HEV-infected mice. Combination regimens with RBV showed strong additive activity. The study suggests that HEV clearance may be achieved in immunosuppressed patients by using and further developing this class of direct antiviral drugs.
