title: Performance Evaluation of HBV RNA Real-Time PCR Kits for Quantitative Detection and Clinical Comparison Across Different Detection Systems
abstract: Serum hepatitis B virus (HBV) RNA has emerged as a potential biomarker of residual viral transcriptional activity in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). However, insufficient assay standardization and variability across testing systems limit the reliability and comparability of HBV RNA measurements. This study aimed to verify the analytical performance of a commercial HBV RNA detection assay (Kit A) and assess its methodological comparability with another commercial assay (Kit B) using clinical serum samples under different testing conditions. This study comprised analytical performance verification of Kit A, clinical sample comparison between Kit A and Kit B using contemporaneous fresh samples, long-term frozen samples, and non-contemporaneous refrigerated samples, and an exploratory comparison of amplification platforms. Both kits were tested in parallel on the same amplification instrument using different nucleic acid extraction platforms, with operators blinded to the other reagent’s results, and analyses included qualitative agreement, quantitative bias, and low-concentration detection concordance. title: Chinese Multidisciplinary Expert Consensus on the Management of Precancerous Lesions of Hepatocellular Carcinoma
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. China accounts for nearly half of the global HCC burden, largely because of the high prevalence of hepatitis B virus infection and hepatitis B-related cirrhosis. Accumulating evidence indicates that low-grade dysplastic nodules, high-grade dysplastic nodules, and selected molecular subtypes of hepatocellular adenoma are closely linked to hepatocarcinogenesis and should be considered high-risk precursor lesions with malignant potential. Intervention during the precancerous stage may reduce HCC incidence and mortality, but standardized diagnostic criteria and evidence-based management strategies remain incompletely defined. To address this need, a multidisciplinary panel of Chinese experts developed this consensus on the diagnosis and management of precancerous lesions of HCC. The recommendations integrate recent advances in hepatology with expertise in imaging, pathology, and therapeutic decision-making. Their implementation is intended to support individualized risk assessment and multidisciplinary management, with the broader goal of improving early detection, reducing HCC incidence, and increasing long-term survival.
journal: Journal of Clinical and Translational Hepatology

title: Risk of occupational viral infections during pregnancy in women working in caregiving professions: a systematic review
abstract: A source of exposure to viral infections during pregnancy is through occupation. This review evaluates existing literature on the risk of contracting viral infections (cytomegalovirus (CMV), hepatitis A, B and C viruses, influenza A virus, parvovirus B19, rubella virus and varicella-zoster virus) among pregnant women employed in caregiving professions. A systematic search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane Library and CINAHL databases. All available records to 8 April 2026 were included in the screening. Nine studies were included. Four studies focused on CMV and parvovirus B19, respectively. One study focused on hepatitis B virus. A significantly increased risk of parvovirus B19 infection among pregnant women working with children was observed in two large, low-risk-of-bias cohort studies. In both studies, the risk was more than twofold higher than among pregnant women in occupations without expected contact with children. The risk of CMV infection during pregnancy among women employed in healthcare or childcare was not significantly higher than observed in non-caregiving occupations. We found some evidence of an increased risk of parvovirus B19 infection during pregnancy when employed in childcare professions. Four studies on CMV were identified, but the studies were too small and inconsistent to make firm conclusions. Research on the risk of occupational viral infections in pregnant women remains limited, with a complete absence of studies on hepatitis A and C, influenza A, rubella and varicella-zoster viruses. This review emphasises the need for further investigation in these areas.

title: Streamlining Hepatitis C Treatment: Implementation of a Clinical Pharmacist-Driven Medication Management Program.
abstract: Background Hepatitis C virus (HCV) affects over 3.9 million individuals in the United States and is effectively treated with direct-acting antiviral (DAA) agents. Clinical pharmacists (CPs) may be the ideal provider to bridge gaps in HCV care by selecting appropriate therapy following drug-drug interaction (DDI) review, navigating access barriers, and supporting adherence. Although CP involvement in HCV care has demonstrated clinical value, there is limited literature describing CP workflows, patient interventions, and CP-led programs that support patients from treatment initiation through sustained virologic response at 12 weeks (SVR12). This study aims to quantify and categorize CP-driven enrollments in a Hepatitis C Clinical Program (HCCP) and assess its impact on patient safety, operational, and clinical outcomes. Methods This retrospective descriptive study evaluates a CP-driven HCCP within a health system specialty pharmacy (HSSP) from May 6, 2024 to March 6, 2025. Patients with a referral to the CP for HCV treatment selection, or external patients with a DAA claim at the HSSP, were eligible for enrollment in the program. The HCCP consisted of six points of clinical care: CP therapy selection, medication access and order placement, prescription triage and patient education, follow-up throughout treatment, intervention support, and laboratory monitoring through SVR12. Results A total of 122 patients were enrolled in the HCCP. Most patients were treatment-naïve (90%) and non-cirrhotic (79%). DDIs were identified in 57% of patients, with statin therapy being the most common (46%). Time-to-treatment was 4 days or less for 76% of patients, with an 88% HSSP prescription capture rate. A 97% SVR12 rate was achieved, and 92% of patients completed therapy on time. Conclusion This study highlights the role of the CP in HCV care and their impact on patient safety and clinical and operational outcomes. Results support further development of CP-driven practice changes and support the implementation of a similar program within other HSSPs.

Clinical pharmacists (CPs) may be the ideal provider to bridge gaps in HCV care by selecting appropriate therapy following drug-drug interaction (DDI) review, navigating access barriers, and supporting adherence. Although CP involvement in HCV care has demonstrated clinical value, there is limited literature describing CP workflows, patient interventions, and CP-led programs that support patients from treatment initiation through sustained virologic response at 12 weeks (SVR12). This study aims to quantify and categorize CP-driven enrollments in a Hepatitis C Clinical Program (HCCP) and assess its impact on patient safety, operational, and clinical outcomes. Methods This retrospective descriptive study evaluates a CP-driven HCCP within a health system specialty pharmacy (HSSP) from May 6, 2024 to March 6, 2025. Patients with a referral to the CP for HCV treatment selection, or external patients with a DAA claim at the HSSP, were eligible for enrollment in the program. The HCCP consisted of six points of clinical care: CP therapy selection, medication access and order placement, prescription triage and patient education, follow-up throughout treatment, intervention support, and laboratory monitoring through SVR12. Results A total of 122 patients were enrolled in the HCCP. Most patients were treatment-naïve (90%) and non-cirrhotic (79%). DDIs were identified in 57% of patients, with statin therapy being the most common (46%). Time-to-treatment was 4 days or less for 76% of patients, with an 88% HSSP prescription capture rate. A 97% SVR12 rate was achieved, and 92% of patients completed therapy on time. Conclusion This study highlights the role of the CP in HCV care and their impact on patient safety and clinical and operational outcomes. Results support further development of CP-driven practice changes and support the implementation of a similar program within other HSSPs.

title: Reductions in Advanced Chronic Liver Disease Among People Who Inject Drugs: The ETHOS Engage Study.
abstract: Background and aims Liver disease is a significant risk for people who inject drugs due to the high burden of hepatitis C virus (HCV). There is limited data on the impact of the direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy era on liver disease among people who inject drugs. This study evaluated baseline and longitudinal liver disease in a national cohort of people who inject drugs recruited over three Waves: 2018-2019, 2019-2021, and 2023-2025. Methods The ETHOS Engage Study is an observational cohort of people who inject drugs attending drug treatment clinics and needle and syringe programs in Australia. Participants completed a questionnaire and underwent point-of-care HCV RNA testing (Xpert HCV Viral Load Fingerstick) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) by vibration-controlled transient hepatic elastography (FibroScan). Advanced chronic liver disease was defined by LSM of 10 kPa or above. Results Among all enrolments with a valid LSM (n = 3126, 79% recruited at drug treatment clinics), 11% had advanced chronic liver disease, decreasing from 12.0% (154/1287) in 2018-2019 to 7.9% (66/839) in 2019-2021, and 6.4% (62/967) in 2023-2025. In adjusted analyses, participants recruited between 2019-2021 and 2023-2025 were less likely to have advanced chronic liver disease (vs. 2018-2019; aOR 0.66, 95% CI: 0.48-0.90 and aOR 0.56, 95% CI: 0.40-0.77, respectively). Current HCV infection declined from 24% in 2018-2019 to 10% in 2023-2025. Among participants with LSM in more than one wave and current HCV infection at first visit and no current HCV infection at second visit (n = 44), advanced chronic liver disease declined from 19% to 5%. Conclusions Unrestricted access to DAA therapies in Australia has been associated with reduced liver disease burden among people who inject drugs. Monitoring of liver health in this population is important, given potential ageing and non-HCV liver disease impacts.

title: Downhill Esophageal Varices Caused by Arteriovenous Fistula: A Case Report
abstract: Background Esophageal varices are classified by the direction of blood flow as uphill or downhill. In downhill esophageal varices, flow is directed from the oral side toward the anal side, and the condition is uncommon, being detected in approximately 0.5% of gastroscopies. The pathogenesis of downhill esophageal varices is diverse and the underlying cause is often difficult to identify. Case presentation A 59-year-old woman was incidentally found to have severe esophageal varices during a routine health examination. She had no haematemesis or melena and no history of liver cirrhosis, and her liver function tests were normal, although she was positive for hepatitis B surface antigen. Varices involved both the proximal and the distal esophagus. Computed tomography angiography showed tortuous, dilated esophageal and gastric fundal veins together with dilated vessels in the lower neck. A first interventional angiogram showed early venous filling only; three months later, a second angiogram demonstrated a fistula between the left inferior thyroid artery and the esophageal vein, at the site of previous thyroid surgery. A diagnosis of downhill esophageal varices caused by an arteriovenous fistula was made, and the patient was followed up with comprehensive evaluation. Conclusions Downhill esophageal varices may result from an arteriovenous fistula even in the absence of superior vena cava obstruction, and are readily mistaken for uphill varices related to portal hypertension, particularly in patients with hepatitis B. Varices that predominate in the upper or middle esophagus, or that persist after a normal portal hypertension work-up, should prompt evaluation of the cervical and mediastinal vasculature.

title: BEYOND THE WHOOP: EXTREME LEUKOCYTOSIS, APNEA, AND CYANOSIS IN AN INFANT WITH PCR-CONFIRMED PERTUSSIS
abstract: Background: Pertussis can cause severe disease in young infants before primary immunization. Classic inspiratory whoop may be absent, while apnea, cyanosis, and marked leukocytosis can dominate the presentation and lead to diagnostic diversion. We report a young infant with PCR-confirmed pertussis whose extreme leukocytosis initially raised concern for hematologic malignancy. Case Presentation Summary: A 2-month-old boy presented with progressive paroxysmal cough associated with respiratory distress, apnea, facial flushing, and perioral cyanosis. His illness began with fever followed by dry cough that increased in frequency and severity. During an earlier hospitalization, he required supplemental oxygen up to 3 L/min and experienced two generalized seizure-like episodes lasting less than two minutes, suspected to represent hypoxic events associated with severe coughing episodes. Leukocytosis exceeding 70,000/μL prompted referral to an oncology center for suspected hematologic malignancy; peripheral blood examination, however, showed no evidence of malignancy. Persistent paroxysmal cough with apnea and cyanosis raised suspicion for pertussis, subsequently confirmed by Bordetella pertussis PCR. Chest radiography demonstrated bilateral pulmonary opacities consistent with pneumonia. During subsequent hospitalization, the leukocyte count decreased to 30,100/μL. The infant had received hepatitis B vaccine but had not yet received a pertussis-containing vaccine. He received azithromycin for seven days, supplemental oxygen, and supportive care, with gradual clinical improvement. Learning Points Discussion: In young infants, the absence of a classic whoop should not lower suspicion for pertussis when paroxysmal cough is accompanied by apnea, cyanosis, and marked leukocytosis. Extreme leukocytosis may mimic hematologic malignancy and divert the initial diagnostic pathway. Recognizing this constellation can facilitate timely molecular testing and appropriate management. The occurrence of severe disease before receipt of primary pertussis immunization also highlights the vulnerable period before vaccine-derived protection is established and reinforces the importance of strategies that protect infants during early life.

title: Severe Hageman factor (factor XII) deficiency discovered during evaluation of palpitations and chest pain: A case report
abstract: BACKGROUND Factor XII (FXII), or Hageman factor, deficiency is a rare, usually autosomal recessive, defect of the contact pathway of coagulation. It characteristically causes a markedly prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) with a normal prothrombin time (PT) and no bleeding tendency, and it is usually discovered incidentally on preoperative or routine screening. Whether FXII deficiency has any clinical consequence, including thrombosis, remains debated, and reports of symptomatic patients usually involve a confirmed thrombotic event. CASE SUMMARY A 36-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B on antiviral therapy, hyperlipidemia and prediabetes presented to the emergency department after two brief episodes, on separate days, of palpitations, mild (2/10) burning left-sided chest pain and shortness of breath; his smartwatch recorded a heart rate of 118 beats per minute during one episode. The symptoms had resolved on arrival. Vital signs, troponin, chest radiograph and electrocardiogram (sinus rhythm with possible right ventricular hypertrophy) showed no acute abnormality. The APTT was > 400 seconds on two measurements with a normal PT and international normalized ratio. A mixing study corrected the APTT, favoring a factor deficiency over an inhibitor, and antiphospholipid testing was normal. FXII activity was < 1% on repeat testing, whereas factors IX and XI, high-molecular-weight kininogen, prekallikrein and von Willebrand parameters were normal. Severe FXII deficiency was diagnosed. No bleeding or thrombosis occurred, symptoms did not recur during telemetry observation, and no treatment was required. The patient was discharged with hematology follow-up and a recommendation for family testing. CONCLUSION In this patient, severe FXII deficiency was an incidental finding and is not considered the cause of the transient symptoms, which remained unexplained. A markedly prolonged isolated APTT warrants a systematic evaluation with mixing studies and factor assays, but the result must be interpreted in the full clinical context, and the patient's symptoms should be evaluated independently rather than attributed prematurely to the laboratory abnormality.

title: Public Health Action against Cancer across Awareness, Primary Prevention and Early Detection: Evidence, Equity and Implementation
abstract: Background: Cancer remains a leading cause of death worldwide, and its burden is shifting towards countries with the least capacity to diagnose and treat it. Public health action, including the promotion of awareness, primary prevention and early detection, is widely presented as the most efficient response, yet the evidence supporting each component differs substantially in type, strength and transferability. Objectives: This critical narrative review examines what public health interventions in cancer awareness, primary prevention, screening and early diagnosis of symptomatic disease have been shown to achieve, where the evidence is contested, and how equity and implementation conditions shape population benefit. Methods: Literature published between January 2000 and September 2026 was identified through structured searches of biomedical and multidisciplinary scholarly databases, authoritative institutional repositories and citation tracking. Randomised trials, quasi-experimental policy evaluations, cohort and registry studies, modelling studies, systematic reviews and consensus statements were appraised qualitatively for design appropriateness, outcome relevance, risk of bias and transferability, and synthesised thematically. Results: The strongest population-level evidence supports fiscal and regulatory tobacco control, vaccination against human papillomavirus and hepatitis B virus, and organised cervical and colorectal screening. Evidence for alcohol pricing and labelling is persuasive but rests mainly on non-cancer or intermediate outcomes. Symptom-awareness campaigns change knowledge and referral activity, but their effects on stage at diagnosis are small and their effects on mortality remain undemonstrated. Breast, lung and prostate screening produce disease-specific mortality benefits that depend heavily on risk targeting, programme quality and the handling of overdiagnosis, while effects on all-cause mortality are rarely detectable. Multi-cancer blood tests and artificial intelligence have advanced faster than evidence of patient benefit. Across the continuum, socioeconomic gradients in exposure, participation and stage at diagnosis recur, and coverage in many low- and middle-income settings remains far below that required for population impact. Conclusions: Public health cancer control is most defensible when it prioritises structural prevention and organised, quality-assured early detection, judges new technologies against mortality and harm outcomes, and treats equitable reach as a primary outcome rather than an afterthought.

Objectives: This critical narrative review examines what public health interventions in cancer awareness, primary prevention, screening and early diagnosis of symptomatic disease have been shown to achieve, where the evidence is contested, and how equity and implementation conditions shape population benefit. Methods: Literature published between January 2000 and September 2026 was identified through structured searches of biomedical and multidisciplinary scholarly databases, authoritative institutional repositories and citation tracking. Randomised trials, quasi-experimental policy evaluations, cohort and registry studies, modelling studies, systematic reviews and consensus statements were appraised qualitatively for design appropriateness, outcome relevance, risk of bias and transferability, and synthesised thematically. Results: The strongest population-level evidence supports fiscal and regulatory tobacco control, vaccination against human papillomavirus and hepatitis B virus, and organised cervical and colorectal screening. Evidence for alcohol pricing and labelling is persuasive but rests mainly on non-cancer or intermediate outcomes. Symptom-awareness campaigns change knowledge and referral activity, but their effects on stage at diagnosis are small and their effects on mortality remain undemonstrated. Breast, lung and prostate screening produce disease-specific mortality benefits that depend heavily on risk targeting, programme quality and the handling of overdiagnosis, while effects on all-cause mortality are rarely detectable. Multi-cancer blood tests and artificial intelligence have advanced faster than evidence of patient benefit. Across the continuum, socioeconomic gradients in exposure, participation and stage at diagnosis recur, and coverage in many low- and middle-income settings remains far below that required for population impact. Conclusions: Public health cancer control is most defensible when it prioritises structural prevention and organised, quality-assured early detection, judges new technologies against mortality and harm outcomes, and treats equitable reach as a primary outcome rather than an afterthought.

title: Real-World Effectiveness and Safety of Sofosbuvir-Based Therapy in Chinese Children and Adolescents With Chronic HCV Infection: A Retrospective Multicentre Study.
abstract: Few direct-acting antiviral regimens are approved in China for children and adolescents with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection and data are limited on their efficacy and safety in this population. This retrospective, multi-centre study aimed to assess the real-world effectiveness and safety of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir (LDV/SOF) and sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (SOF/VEL) in Chinese paediatric patients. The study included patients aged 3-17 years from five hospitals across China who received either LDV/SOF or SOF/VEL for chronic HCV infection. The outcomes included the proportion of patients who achieved sustained virologic response at 12 weeks post-treatment (SVR12), normalisation rates of ALT and AST levels, and incidence of adverse events (AEs). A total of 129 patients from five sites were included and 128 completed 12 weeks of post-treatment follow-up. Mean age was 9.9 years (standard deviation, 3.9), with 30 (23.3%), 55 (42.6%), and 44 (34.1%) patients aged 3-6, 7-11, and 12-17 years, respectively, 84 (65.1%) were male, 62 (48.1%) were infected with genotype 3, and baseline ALT and AST levels were elevated in 64 (49.6%) and 75 (58.1%) patients, respectively. The SVR12 rate was 98.4% (126/128) in the overall population, remaining consistent across subgroups by sex, age, HCV genotype, or regimen. ALT and AST levels were normalised in all patients with available data. AEs were reported by 16.4% (21/128) of patients and none were serious. Collectively, this study demonstrated that LDV/SOF and SOF/VEL were highly effective and well tolerated in Chinese paediatric patients with chronic HCV infection.

title: Associations Between Self-Reported Previous Hepatitis C Diagnosis, Hepatitis C Treatment, and Current Binge Drinking Among Persons Who Inject Drugs-National HIV Behavioural Surveillance, 2015-2024.
abstract: Persons who inject drugs (PWID) are disproportionately affected by hepatitis C virus (HCV). Excessive alcohol use among PWID can lead to more rapid progression of liver disease among persons with HCV. We assessed associations between ever reporting HCV infection, ever reporting HCV treatment, and current binge drinking among PWID who participated in National HIV Behavioural Surveillance (NHBS) during 2015-2024. NHBS conducted biobehavioural surveys among PWID using respondent-driven sampling in 2015, 2018, 2022, and 2024. We estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) to assess the association between self-report of ever having HCV infection, HCV treatment, and binge drinking in the past 30 days. The percentage of PWID reporting binge drinking was 25.8% in 2015, 24.0% in 2018, 13.3% in 2022, and 17.2% in 2024. In adjusted analysis, we found a significant negative relationship between self-reported ever having HCV infection and binge drinking in the past 30 days in three of the four surveys: 2018 (aPR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.83-0.99), 2022 (aPR: 0.79, 95% CI:0.70-0.90), and 2024 (aPR:0.78, 95% CI: 0.65-0.93). We did not find significant associations between previously ever receiving treatment for HCV infection and binge drinking in the past 30 days across the four survey years. Among PWID, HCV infection was associated with reduced prevalence of binge drinking in 2018, 2022, and 2024. Our results support the importance of testing PWID for HCV infection and continued education on the harms associated with excessive alcohol use, including among persons who have received treatment for HCV infection.

title: Enhancing the Hepatitis C Cascade of Care: Implementation Science Approach in a Federally Qualified Health Center System.
abstract: Context Hepatitis C virus (HCV) remains a significant public health challenge in the United States, particularly among underserved populations. Despite curative treatments, systemic barriers often delay the care cascade. Program This quality improvement program aimed at improving the care of patients with chronic Hepatitis C within a Federally Qualified Health Center system in Southern California, known as AltaMed Health Services. The program involves AltaMed, serving more than 700 000 patients, primarily low-income people in underserved communities through an integrated delivery system for Latino and multiethnic individuals, focusing on enhancing screening and treatment processes for Hepatitis C. Methods A multipronged clinical workflow redesign was evaluated utilizing the RE-AIM framework to assess process and clinical between 2022 and 2024. Intervention included an electronic health record (EHR) Best Practice Advisory to identify patients due for HCV screening, a standardized direct-referral workflow, and a Linkage to Care team to manage prior authorization administrative tasks and patient outreach efforts. Evaluation Total descriptive HCV screening volumes increased from 30 212 to 47 951, with screening rates expanding from 3.4% to 7.3% in nonspecialty clinics. Treatment initiation rates shifted from 36% to 45%, and post-treatment patient outreach documentation changed from 48% to 73%. The average duration from diagnosis to treatment initiation was observed to be 55.9% lower, changing from 34 weeks in 2022 and 15 weeks in 2024. Discussion Establishing an Linkage to Care team, combined with automated EHR tools, can track alongside meaningful improvements in the safety-net HCV care cascade. Scaling models require careful consideration of specialized staffing and localized EHR infrastructure to advance health equity and global HCV elimination goals.

title: National and Regional Trends in Childhood Vaccination Coverage in Türkiye, 1985–2025: An Ecological Time Series Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: National averages may conceal regional declines in childhood vaccination. I described trends in administrative coverage published for Türkiye and its regions through 2025. Methods: Coverage of the third diphtheria–pertussis–tetanus dose (DPT3), BCG, third hepatitis B dose (HBV3), first measles-containing dose (MCV1) and pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) was extracted from Ministry of Health publications. Joinpoint regression with Bonferroni adjustment was applied to the 12 NUTS-1 regions for 2002–2025 and repeated for 2009–2025, 2019–2025 and alternative specifications. Results: In 2025, national coverage was 94% for DPT3, 93% for BCG and 92% for MCV1 and the PCV booster. Regional indicators rose steeply until joinpoints in 2006–2012, years that overlap schedule and reporting changes. Later slopes were mostly negative; in the principal models, six DPT3 or MCV1 declines met the adjusted threshold in 2009–2025, all in Central Anatolia, Western Anatolia and the Black Sea regions, and none in the other windows. MCV1 declines in Central Anatolia and Western Black Sea persisted under every specification. BCG declined in the same regions; all PCV booster slopes were negative, none meeting the threshold. Units reporting at least 95% coverage fell from 80 to 32 of 81 for DPT3 and from 75 to 19 for MCV1 during 2013–2025; the 2018 survey DPT3 estimate was 19 points below the administrative value. Conclusions: Published coverage has plateaued and, in central and Black Sea regions, declined slowly, most consistently for MCV1. Its link to true uptake is uncertain. Active recall in these regions, a national coverage survey and a denominator audit are needed.

Methods: Coverage of the third diphtheria–pertussis–tetanus dose (DPT3), BCG, third hepatitis B dose (HBV3), first measles-containing dose (MCV1) and pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) was extracted from Ministry of Health publications. Joinpoint regression with Bonferroni adjustment was applied to the 12 NUTS-1 regions for 2002–2025 and repeated for 2009–2025, 2019–2025 and alternative specifications. Results: In 2025, national coverage was 94% for DPT3, 93% for BCG and 92% for MCV1 and the PCV booster. Regional indicators rose steeply until joinpoints in 2006–2012, years that overlap schedule and reporting changes. Later slopes were mostly negative; in the principal models, six DPT3 or MCV1 declines met the adjusted threshold in 2009–2025, all in Central Anatolia, Western Anatolia and the Black Sea regions, and none in the other windows. MCV1 declines in Central Anatolia and Western Black Sea persisted under every specification. BCG declined in the same regions; all PCV booster slopes were negative, none meeting the threshold. Units reporting at least 95% coverage fell from 80 to 32 of 81 for DPT3 and from 75 to 19 for MCV1 during 2013–2025; the 2018 survey DPT3 estimate was 19 points below the administrative value. Conclusions: Published coverage has plateaued and, in central and Black Sea regions, declined slowly, most consistently for MCV1. Its link to true uptake is uncertain. Active recall in these regions, a national coverage survey and a denominator audit are needed.

title: Multivariate spatiotemporal using INLA: analysis of sexually transmitted infections in West Java, Indonesia
abstract: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs), including human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and hepatitis B/C, pose a significant public health challenge in Indonesia, particularly in West Java, the country’s most populous province. This study seeks to analyze the spatiotemporal distribution of STIs to enhance disease management strategies. Spatiotemporal multivariate M-models utilizing integrated nested laplace approximation (INLA) inference were applied to the Indonesian National Health Insurance data covering the period from 2015 to 2022 in West Java. Fifteen models were developed based on three spatial models, each paired with a temporal prior and five interaction types. The analysis identified the proper conditional autoregressive model with temporal interaction (pCAR type 2) as the best-performing model. This model revealed distinct temporal patterns in each region that did not influence neighboring areas. Notably, the posterior mean relative risk for HIV and hepatitis B/C was found to be higher in northern West Java (>1.00); however, the region most at risk for each infection differs, partially due to a lack of correlation between HIV and hepatitis B/C (\rho=-0.15). These findings underscore the need for customized mitigation strategies tailored to specific diseases and regional differences in risk patterns.

title: Sustainable Bio-Medical Waste Management in India: Issues and Emerging Challenges1
abstract: Improper Bio-Medical Waste Management or health care waste leads to many problems particularly diseases like, Hepatitis B and C, Tetanus, Human Immune Deficiency Virus (HIV), and many more, recent days hospitals, clinics, health care institutions, blood banks, labs, and research institutions are generating large quantity of Bio-Medical Waste, (hereinafter called as BMW) as per the annual report, 2023 published by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), nearly more than 743 tons of Bio-Medical Waste generated per day even it has been increased significantly compared to previous years, this data shows that in near future India will surpass approximately more than 1000 tons of Bio-Medical Waste per day before 2030.

title: Liver Transplantation for Hepatitis E Virus–Associated Acute Liver Failure in the Presence of HEV RNAemia: A Brief report and Literature Review
abstract: Abstract Hepatitis E virus (HEV) genotypes 3 and 4 can cause chronic hepatitis in solid organ transplant recipients, potentially progressing to cirrhosis. Liver transplantation for fulminant HEV infection is rarely reported, particularly in the setting of ongoing viremia. We report the case of a 63-year-old man with acute HEV-induced liver failure superimposed on steatotic liver disease who underwent urgent liver transplantation despite ongoing HEV RNAemia. Ribavirin therapy was initiated before transplantation, but HEV RNA remained detectable until day 32 post-transplant, consistent with early allograft infection. Antiviral therapy was continued for two weeks after viral clearance, and no relapse occurred following treatment discontinuation. This case, together with the limited published literature, demonstrates that liver transplantation during ongoing HEV RNAemia is feasible when combined with prolonged peri- and post-transplant antiviral therapy and close virological monitoring. Detectable HEV RNAemia should therefore not preclude liver transplantation in patients with fulminant HEV infection.

title: Climate Change as a Driver of Aflatoxin Contamination in Nigerian Staple Foods: Emerging Health Risks and Prevention Strategies
abstract: Aflatoxin contamination is a persistent food safety concern in Nigeria, where maize, groundnuts and other staple crops are widely consumed and may be exposed to changing climatic and storage conditions. This narrative review examines how climate change and climate variability may influence aflatoxin occurrence, dietary exposure, health outcomes and prevention options in Nigerian food systems. Peer-reviewed studies and institutional documents were synthesised thematically, with evidence differentiated as established mechanisms, observational associations, modelled projections or evidence gaps. The reviewed literature identifies drought and heat stress during crop development, irregular rainfall and humid post-harvest environments as plausible drivers of fungal colonisation and aflatoxin production. However, the magnitude and direction of these effects vary by crop, agroecological zone and stage of the supply chain. Available crop-model projections indicate increased aflatoxin contamination risk for Nigerian maize under future climate scenarios, whereas groundnut projections are model-dependent and remain insufficiently validated. Chronic aflatoxin exposure has a well-established association with hepatocellular carcinoma, particularly among people with hepatitis B infection; evidence concerning childhood growth impairment and other health outcomes is less conclusive. Nigerian studies rarely connect measured weather conditions, food contamination, exposure biomarkers and clinical outcomes within the same design. Prevention therefore requires coordinated pre-harvest biocontrol, timely drying, suitable storage, testing, surveillance and risk-based regulatory enforcement. Climate-linked monitoring and locally evaluated interventions remain priorities for strengthening food safety without overstating the available causal evidence.

title: Rat Hepatitis E Virus Circulation in Brown Rats from 8 Cities, France, 2021–2023
abstract: Rat hepatitis E virus (rHEV) is a zoonotic pathogen responsible for acute or chronic hepatitis in humans. To assess rHEV circulation in brown rats (Rattus norvegicus) in France, we sampled animals in 8 cities. We detected rHEV RNA in livers of 209/686 rats, a 30.5% positivity rate (95% CI 27.1%-34.0%). We found rHEV-positive animals in all 8 cities; positivity rate range was 9.7% (95% CI 6.7%-13.8%) to 44% (95% CI 33.9%-55.3%). Positivity rate differed by weight class: 9% (95% CI 5.8%-13.8%) in rats 100 g. We detected rHEV antibodies in 144/317 (45% [95% CI 40.0%-51.0%]) of the samples. We obtained 20 full genome sequences with distinct rHEV strains. We observed high genetic identity between rat and human sequences in France and Europe. rHEV appears to be enzootic in rat populations in cities in France.

title: Association of HBeAg status with serum biomarkers and cardiac profiles in patients with hepatic tumors: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection has been associated with extrahepatic manifestations, including cardiac abnormalities. Whether hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) status is associated with distinct serum biomarker profiles and echocardiographic phenotypes in patients with malignant hepatic tumors remains unclear. Methods In this retrospective study, 380 patients with malignant hepatic tumors were stratified into HBsAg-negative controls (n = 67), HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B (CHB) with hepatic tumors (n = 224), and HBeAg-positive CHB with hepatic tumors (n = 89). Serum tumor markers (AFP, CEA, CA19-9, CA242, DCP, AFP-L3%) and cardiac/inflammatory biomarkers (NT-proBNP, PCT, c-TnT) were measured. Echocardiographic indices, including E/A inversion and E/A < 0.8, were available in a small subset. Unadjusted Kruskal–Wallis or categorical tests were used for group comparisons. AFP and DCP were additionally analyzed individually and jointly using multinomial logistic regression with patient-clustered standard errors, with and without adjustment for sex. Results HBeAg-positive patients were significantly younger and more predominantly male than the other groups. AFP and DCP were each associated with serological group when assessed alone (P = 0.00046 and P = 0.0014, respectively), and the joint test was also significant (P = 0.00017). The joint association persisted after adjustment for sex (P = 0.00036), with no significant sex main effect (P = 0.2258) or marker-by-sex interaction (P = 0.3737). NT-proBNP was higher in both HBV-infected groups than in controls, but this finding was not adjusted for renal function, age, or cardiac comorbidities. Although E/A inversion and E/A < 0.8 were less frequent in the HBeAg-positive group, this group was substantially younger, and E/A alone is insufficient to diagnose diastolic dysfunction. These echocardiographic findings are therefore exploratory and hypothesis-generating and cannot establish an independent association. Conclusions HBeAg status was associated with distinct demographic and biomarker profiles in patients with malignant hepatic tumors. AFP and DCP were associated with HBeAg status individually and jointly, and no significant sex interaction was observed. The echocardiographic findings were based on a small, selected subgroup with marked age differences and should be regarded as exploratory only. No independent or causal inference can be drawn regarding HBeAg status and cardiac function. Larger, age-matched, homogeneous cohorts with comprehensive echocardiographic assessment and prespecified multivariable models are required for validation.

title: Hepatitis aguda de patrón hepatocelular asociada a infección primaria por virus de Epstein-Barr en una mujer inmunocompetente: reporte de caso
abstract: Introducción: La afectación hepática asociada a infección aguda por virus de Epstein-Barr es frecuente, aunque generalmente cursa con elevaciones leves y autolimitadas de las aminotransferasas. La hepatitis aguda clínicamente manifiesta como forma predominante de presentación constituye una manifestación menos habitual y puede representar un reto diagnóstico. Presentación del caso: Mujer de 25 años, inmunocompetente, con antecedente de hipotiroidismo primario y síndrome ovárico metabólico poliendócrino, quien presentó síndrome febril de 12 días de evolución asociado a dolor en hipocondrio derecho. Durante su evaluación se documentó leucocitosis con linfocitosis absoluta marcada, hepatoesplenomegalia y elevación significativa de aminotransferasas con patrón predominantemente hepatocelular (AST 417 U/L, ALT 833 U/L), bilirrubinas normales y función sintética hepática conservada. Inicialmente se consideraron diversas etiologías infecciosas y hepatobiliares; sin embargo, la presencia de hepatoesplenomegalia y linfocitosis orientó la sospecha hacia infección por VEB. Los estudios serológicos mostraron anticuerpos anti-VCA IgM y anti-VCA IgG positivos, con EBNA negativo, compatibles con infección aguda por VEB. Se descartaron infección por VIH, hepatitis B y hepatitis C. La tomografía abdominal evidenció hepatomegalia y esplenomegalia sin datos de obstrucción biliar. La paciente recibió tratamiento de soporte, con evolución clínica favorable y descenso progresivo de las alteraciones hematológicas y bioquímicas durante la hospitalización y el seguimiento ambulatorio. Conclusiones: La infección aguda por VEB debe considerarse dentro del diagnóstico diferencial de pacientes jóvenes con síndrome febril, hepatoesplenomegalia, linfocitosis y hepatitis aguda, incluso en ausencia de las manifestaciones clásicas de mononucleosis infecciosa. El reconocimiento oportuno de esta entidad puede contribuir a orientar adecuadamente el abordaje diagnóstico diferencial.

title: Disparities in the gastrointestinal cancer burden across country income levels: a population-based study from 1990 to 2023
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers represent a major global health burden. Socioeconomic context, approximated by country income level, is an important aggregate indicator associated with cancer outcomes and may reflect differences in risk factor exposure, healthcare access, and diagnostic capacity. This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate global patterns and trends in the incidence and mortality of GI cancers across the economic gradient. In this population-based study, data on six GI cancers (liver, colorectum, stomach, esophagus, pancreas, and gallbladder/biliary tract) were extracted from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 study from 1990 to 2023. Countries were categorized into four World Bank income groups: high-income countries (HICs), upper-middle-income countries (UMICs), lower-middle-income countries (LMICs), and low-income countries (LICs). Primary metrics analyzed included age-standardized incidence rates (ASIR) and age-standardized death rates (ASDR). The burden of GI cancers showed distinct patterns across income levels. In 2023, LICs recorded the highest ASIR and ASDR for liver cancer, while HICs showed an increasing ASIR trend from 1990 to 2023, driven primarily by hepatitis C, alcohol consumption, and hepatitis B. The ASIR of colorectal cancer was highest in HICs; however, CRC mortality significantly declined in HICs, while ASDR increased in LMICs and LICs. The gastric cancer burden was highest in UMICs. Esophageal cancer exhibited an inverse relationship with country income level, with the highest ASIR and ASDR observed in LICs. Pancreatic and gallbladder cancers exhibited the highest ASIRs in HICs. Risk-attributable analysis revealed dietary risks as the leading contributor to GI cancer burden in HICs and LICs, while tobacco use predominated in UMICs and LMICs. Overall, this study reveals significant global inequalities in GI cancer burden across economic strata. LICs face a disproportionate mortality burden from highly fatal cancers such as liver and esophageal cancer, driven by high-risk exposure and limited care access. Conversely, HICs report high incidence rates for CRC and pancreatic cancer yet demonstrate notable mortality reductions in CRC, a benefit not yet realized in resource-limited settings. These income-stratified patterns represent associations and may reflect differences in risk exposure, diagnostic capacity, and health-system performance rather than income itself.

source_records.title: Disparities in the gastrointestinal cancer burden across country income levels: a population-based study from 1990 to 2023
source_records.abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers represent a major global health burden. Socioeconomic context, approximated by country income level, is an important aggregate indicator associated with cancer outcomes and may reflect differences in risk factor exposure, healthcare access, and diagnostic capacity. This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate global patterns and trends in the incidence and mortality of GI cancers across the economic gradient. In this population-based study, data on six GI cancers (liver, colorectum, stomach, esophagus, pancreas, and gallbladder/biliary tract) were extracted from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 study from 1990 to 2023. Countries were categorized into four World Bank income groups: high-income countries (HICs), upper-middle-income countries (UMICs), lower-middle-income countries (LMICs), and low-income countries (LICs). Primary metrics analyzed included age-standardized incidence rates (ASIR) and age-standardized death rates (ASDR). The burden of GI cancers showed distinct patterns across income levels. In 2023, LICs recorded the highest ASIR and ASDR for liver cancer, while HICs showed an increasing ASIR trend from 1990 to 2023, driven primarily by hepatitis C, alcohol consumption, and hepatitis B. The ASIR of colorectal cancer was highest in HICs; however, CRC mortality significantly declined in HICs, while ASDR increased in LMICs and LICs. The gastric cancer burden was highest in UMICs. Esophageal cancer exhibited an inverse relationship with country income level, with the highest ASIR and ASDR observed in LICs. Pancreatic and gallbladder cancers exhibited the highest ASIRs in HICs. Risk-attributable analysis revealed dietary risks as the leading contributor to GI cancer burden in HICs and LICs, while tobacco use predominated in UMICs and LMICs. Conversely, HICs report high incidence rates for CRC and pancreatic cancer yet demonstrate notable mortality reductions in CRC, a benefit not yet realized in resource-limited settings. These income-stratified patterns represent associations and may reflect differences in risk exposure, diagnostic capacity, and health-system performance rather than income itself.

title: Factors Associated With Compliance With Triple Elimination Screening
abstract: The main benefit of Triple Elimination screening is to break the chain of transmission of HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B from mother to child. If Triple Elimination screening is not performed, the risk of vertical transmission of these diseases remains high. Based on the 2025 report from Sungai Menang Public Health Center, of the 340 pregnant women recorded as attending antenatal care visits, 204 women (60%) had not completed Triple Elimination screening. This study aims to determine the factors related to compliance with Triple Elimination screening at Sungai Menang Public Health Center, Ogan Komering Ilir (OKI) Regency. This study employed an analytical research design with a cross-sectional approach. The study was conducted at Sungai Menang Public Health Center, Ogan Komering Ilir Regency, from April 17 to 30, 2026. The study sample consisted of all pregnant women who visited Sungai Menang Public Health Center in April 2026, totaling 42 women. Total sampling was used. Data were analyzed using univariate and bivariate analyses with the Chi-Square test. The results showed that 18 respondents (42.9%) had good knowledge, 26 respondents (61.9%) received support from their husbands, and 25 respondents (59.5%) had high motivation. There were significant relationships between knowledge (p = 0.001), family support (p = 0.025), and maternal motivation (p = 0.025) and compliance with Triple Elimination screening at Sungai Menang Public Health Center. The researcher recommends that Sungai Menang Public Health Center improve the quality of healthcare services, particularly the Triple Elimination program, by strengthening health education and counseling activities for pregnant women and providing effective and continuous counseling.

title: A multiscale model for hepatitis C virus infection with spatial heterogeneity and nonlocal diffusion under general incidences
abstract: Intracellular processes play a fundamental role in immune activation, suggesting that multiscale modeling is necessary to capture their impact on within-host viral dynamics. In this paper, we propose a multiscale mathematical model for the within-host dynamics of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection that incorporates spatial heterogeneity, nonlocal diffusion of viral particles, and general incidence functions. The model describes the interactions between healthy hepatocytes, infected cells, intracellular viral RNA, free virions, and the adaptive immune response, including both cytotoxic T lymphocytes and antibodies. The movement of virions within the liver is modeled through a nonlocal dispersal operator characterized by a symmetric probability kernel. The growth of healthy hepatocytes is governed by a general class of functions. We first establish the well-posedness of the model by proving the existence, uniqueness, positivity, and global boundedness of solutions. Moreover, we show that the induced semiflow is asymptotically smooth and admits a compact global attractor. Using the next-generation operator approach, we define the basic reproduction number R0 and characterize its threshold role in the infection dynamics. In particular, we prove that the infection-free equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable when R0 1. Finally, we present some numerical simulations to confirm the obtained theoretical results.

title: Update in alternative donor strategies in heart and lung transplantation.
abstract: Purpose of review Alternative donor strategies in cardiothoracic transplantation are becoming routine. This review covers recent developments and their implications for the anesthesiologist. Recent findings Donor scarcity is a principal constraint on heart and lung transplantation. Donation after circulatory death (DCD) and the adoption of machine preservation have reshaped the donor pool. This review covers literature comparing thoracoabdominal normothermic regional perfusion with direct procurement and preservation, warm ischemic thresholds and their relationship to primary graft dysfunction, normothermic and hypothermic ex-situ perfusion, 10 °C static cold storage, and ex-vivo lung perfusion, and discusses the ethics of DCD. Extended-criteria and hepatitis C virus-viremic donors are now used routinely, and cardiac xenotransplantation is entering clinical study. Each advance alters graft physiology at reperfusion and the timing of perioperative services. Research into cardiac xenotransplantation is ongoing. Summary These strategies enlarge the donor pool and introduce novel graft physiological concerns, as well as ethical concerns, for the anesthesiologist.

title: Serological Evidence of Hepatitis E Virus Exposure in Swine in Northern and Central Kazakhstan
abstract: The study of hepatitis E virus (HEV) in pigs is of considerable epizootiological and epidemiological importance because of the pathogen’s zoonotic potential and pigs’ established role as a natural reservoir. Investigating the prevalence, patterns of viral circulation, and genetic diversity of HEV helps assess the potential risk of transmission to humans, including through food products of animal origin. In Kazakhstan, seroprevalence of hepatitis E virus (HEV) in swine has never been investigated. Hepatitis E virus genotypes associated with pigs are zoonotic and may circulate silently in swine herds. We assessed serological evidence of HEV exposure and screened for HEV RNA in samples collected from clinically healthy pigs in northern and central Kazakhstan during 2025–2026. In total, 164 specimens (78 rectal swabs and 86 blood specimens) were examined by qRT-PCR, and sera or plasma from 86 pigs were tested for anti-HEV antibodies using the ID Screen Hepatitis E Indirect Multi-species ELISA. Seven of 164 specimens (4.3%) were presumptively positive by qRT-PCR. The serological assay revealed that 44/86 animals were ELISA-positive (51.2%; 95% CI, 40.8–61.5), 11/86 were equivocal (12.8%), and 31/86 were negative (36.0%). These findings provide initial evidence of substantial HEV exposure in the sampled herds and a potential threat to the human population. The findings are essential for improving epizootiological surveillance, developing preventive measures, and ensuring biological safety within the framework of the One Health approach.

title: Hepatitis E Virus Exposure in a Selected Cohort of Norwegian Semi-Domesticated Reindeer (Rangifer tarandus tarandus): A Longitudinal Study
abstract: Semi-domesticated reindeer (Rangifer tarandus tarandus) are free-ranging but interact closely with humans during round-ups and slaughter. They are exposed to a range of pathogens, some of which are zoonotic. We investigated Hepatitis E virus (HEV) seroprevalence in a purposively selected cohort of 111 animals from three geographically distinct Norwegian semi-domesticated reindeer herds over more than two consecutive years, with a subset of animals followed longitudinally from approximately 7 to 33 months of age. We observed total anti-HEV antibodies in 28 of 322 (8.7%) serum samples collected from 23 individual reindeer, corresponding to a cumulative seropositivity of 20.7% (23/111). The highest proportion of seropositive reindeer was detected in Mo i Rana (31.7%), followed by Tana (23.5%) and Røros (5.6%). Seropositive reindeer were detected in all age groups, but seroprevalence was significantly higher in the 19–21-month (16.7%) than in the 7–9-month age group (8.3%). Fecal samples and/or rectal swabs from some seropositive animals were analyzed for HEV RNA using real-time RT-qPCR, but no HEV RNA was detected. Our findings suggest exposure to HEV or an antigenically related virus in Norwegian reindeer and highlight the need for further studies to identify the virus and investigate infection in animals and humans that interact with reindeer.

title: A Rare Case of ABO-Incompatible Living Donor Liver Transplant in Hyperacute Liver
abstract: Hepatitis A virus (HAV) infection is usually self-limiting; however, acute liver failure (ALF) is a rare, life- threatening complication that may require emergency liver transplantation. When no ABO-compatible donor is available, ABO-incompatible living donor liver transplantation (ABOi-LDLT) may be the only option. However, preformed anti-donor antibodies increase the risk of antibody-mediated rejection, and conventional desensitisation may not be feasible when transplantation cannot be delayed. We report the case of a previously healthy 26-year-old man (blood group O positive) with HAV-related ALF who presented with grade IV hepatic encephalopathy, prothrombin time (international normalised ratio [INR]) 5.64, serum glutamate pyruvate transaminase (SGPT) 4615 U/L, lactate 12 mmol/L, and pH 7.2 (King's College Criteria [KCC] positive). He required intubation, mechanical ventilation, and continuous renal replacement therapy with haemoadsorption. As no compatible donor was available, emergency ABOi-LDLT was performed within 24 hours of admission using a right-lobe graft from his B-positive mother. Preoperative plasma exchange reduced anti-B IgG and IgM titres from 1:128 and 1:64 to 1:16 and 1:4, respectively. Intraoperative splenectomy and rituximab administration in two divided doses (intraoperatively and on postoperative Day 5), along with corticosteroids, triple immunosuppression, and serial antibody titre monitoring, were employed as part of the individualised desensitisation strategy. The postoperative course was complicated by ventilator-associated pneumonia due to carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, which was treated according to culture sensitivity, with temporary withholding of mycophenolate mofetil. A subsequent rise in antibody titres without associated graft dysfunction was managed successfully with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), highlighting the importance of antibody surveillance and tailored postoperative management. The patient was weaned from mechanical ventilation and discharged on postoperative Day 17 with stable graft function and no evidence of rejection. This case demonstrates that emergency ABOi-LDLT may be feasible in selected patients with rapidly progressive ALF when an ABO-compatible donor is unavailable, provided that individualised antibody reduction, close serological monitoring, and vigilant postoperative critical care are available.

title: Efficacy of Bovine Lactoferrin in Chronic Hepatitis C: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
abstract: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection remains a major cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Bovine lactoferrin (bLF), a glycoprotein with antiviral and immunomodulatory properties, has been investigated as a potential therapeutic agent. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy of bLF on virologic and biochemical outcomes in patients with chronic HCV infection. PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through November 5, 2024 (CRD42024621752). Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials comparing bLF with placebo or no treatment. Pooled analyses used a random-effects inverse-variance model. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2, with exploratory subgroup analyses and meta-regression. Five randomized controlled trials were included, four contributing to quantitative analyses. No statistically significant differences were observed for virologic response (RR = 1.00, 95% CI: 0.74-1.36; I2 = 31%), biochemical response (RR = 1.04, 95% CI: 0.71-1.53; I2 = 0%), or sustained virologic response (RR = 1.06, 95% CI: 0.63-1.76; I2 = 0%). Subgroup analyses and meta-regression identified no significant sources of heterogeneity. The available randomized evidence does not demonstrate a statistically significant benefit of bLF on virologic or biochemical responses. Further studies using contemporary treatment strategies and mechanistic endpoints are warranted.

title: Determinants of cancer care delays in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)
abstract: Background Cancer outcomes in sub-Saharan Africa are driven by delayed diagnosis and treatment initiation. We evaluated the magnitude and determinants of diagnostic and treatment delays among cancer patients in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Methods We conducted a hospital-based cross-sectional study of 460 adults with confirmed cancer at Nganda Hospital Center in Kinshasa, DRC. Two outcomes were assessed: delay from symptom onset to diagnosis and delay from diagnosis to treatment initiation. Log-normal regression models were fitted for each outcome to estimate adjusted geometric mean ratios (aGMRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Covariates included demographic, socioeconomic, clinical, behavioral, and stigma-related factors. Results The median age was 55 years, and 76.2% of participants were women. Overall, 55.0% of participants experienced symptom-to-diagnosis delays > 6 months, and 49.4% experienced diagnosis-to-treatment delays > 3 months. Age ≥ 65 years was associated with longer diagnostic delay (aGMR 1.55, 95% CI 1.03–2.31) and age 50–64 years with longer treatment delay (1.51, 1.07–2.14). No work outside the household in the past 7 days was associated with both diagnostic delay (1.68, 1.15–2.47) and treatment delay (2.27, 1.54–3.33). Longer diagnostic delay was additionally associated with informal trading (1.99, 1.21–3.28) and shared taxi or motorbike transport (1.92, 1.25–2.94), while high cancer-stereotype stigma was associated with longer treatment delay (1.56, 1.04–2.34). Associations with hepatitis B infection (diagnostic delay 1.88, 1.06–3.34; treatment delay 2.42, 1.15–5.11) and smoking (diagnostic delay 2.25, 1.03–4.91) were based on small numbers (n = 14 each) and were imprecisely estimated. Conclusions Substantial delays exist across the DRC cancer care continuum and are associated with markers of socioeconomic vulnerability, transport barriers and cancer-related stigma. These findings highlight the need for integrated interventions to improve timely diagnosis and treatment initiation, including strengthening financial protection, decentralizing cancer services, and reducing stigma in cancer care.

title: Examining the Surveillance System for Chronic Hepatitis C among Women of Reproductive Age: Implications for Perinatal HCV Management
abstract: Abstract Objective This study evaluated a jurisdiction’s chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) surveillance system and examined sociodemographic factors associated with confirmed HCV diagnosis among women aged 15–45 years. Methods A convergent mixed-methods design was used. Quantitative analysis included NEDSS surveillance data for women aged 15–45 years reported with HCV in Maryland from 2018–2022. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and logistic regression assessed factors associated with confirmatory diagnosis. Qualitative interviews with public health surveillance personnel were analyzed deductively using the Surveillance Evaluation Framework. Results Among 2,197 women, 62.7% had confirmed diagnoses and 37.3% were probable cases. Women aged 26–35 years were more likely to receive confirmatory diagnosis than those aged 15–25 years (adjusted OR = 1.32; 95% CI: 1.03–1.70). Black women were less likely than White women to receive confirmatory diagnosis (adjusted OR = 0.45; 95% CI: 0.35–0.58). Qualitative findings highlighted strengths including standardized reporting and electronic notification, while challenges included incomplete reporting, interoperability limitations, workforce constraints, and weak perinatal follow-up systems. Conclusions Jurisdiction’s HCV surveillance system supports case reporting and monitoring but faces persistent challenges in data completeness, interoperability, workforce capacity, and identification of perinatally exposed infants. Strengthening surveillance infrastructure, provider reporting, and follow-up for women of reproductive age and exposed infants may improve HCV prevention and elimination efforts.

title: Prevalence and Risk Factors of Hepatitis C Virus Infection Among Garbage Collectors in Tehran, Iran
abstract: Background: Garbage collectors face a heightened risk of exposure to blood borne viruses like Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection. Accurate statistics on HCV prevalence and risk factors among garbage collectors, particularly in Tehran, are lacking. This study aims to determine the prevalence of hepatitis C infection among garbage collectors in Tehran and identify associated risk factors, contributing to a better understanding of their health risks. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted involving 132 unauthorized garbage collectors across 22 districts in Tehran. Participants were selected using cluster sampling, and data were collected through interviews and rapid hepatitis C infection testing. Statistical analyses were performed using univariate and multivariate logistic regression models to identify independent risk factors for hepatitis C infection. Results: The study found that 7.6% of participants tested positive for hepatitis C infection. The mean age was 29.8 years, and approximately 48.5% of those with HCV had no history of addiction, indicating that other exposures such as tattooing in prison and unsafe practices also contributed to infection risk. Significant risk factors identified included a history of tattooing in prison (OR: 10.58, 95%CI: 1.77-63.26, p=0.01). Compared to similar studies, the results of this showed a lower hepatitis C infection prevalence, but higher than that in the general population of Tehran. Conclusion: The high prevalence of hepatitis C infection among Tehran’s garbage collectors underscores the critical need for targeted public health interventions. Efforts should focus on reducing risk behaviors, improving health education, and enhancing disease management. Systemic reforms and better data collection are essential for safeguarding the health of garbage collectors.

title: The properties and safety of hare meat (scientific review) (part 2)
abstract: The hare is a popular hunting trophy, and its meat is widely consumed by hunters and their families, being perceived as an environmentally friendly product. However, fragmentary data on biological and chemical risks pose a threat to consumer health, necessitating a systematisation of information on the infectious, parasitic and toxicological aspects of hare meat safety. A search for relevant publications was conducted using keywords in Scopus, PubMed, eLibrary, Google Scholar and open Internet sources. Works containing data on zoonotic pathogens, helminths, coccidia, as well as on the content of heavy metals (Pb, Cd, Hg, Cr) and pesticides in hare tissues were analysed. The summarised data indicate that hares serve as a reservoir for Francisella tularensis, Yersinia spp., Toxoplasma gondii, Leishmania infantum, hepatitis E virus, as well as for helminths (Trichostrongylus spp. Protostrongylus spp., Taenia pisiformis) and coccidia. In industrially developed regions, exceedances of maximum permissible concentrations of lead (up to 3.53 mg/kg), cadmium (up to 49.12 mg/kg), mercury and chromium have been recorded in the liver and kidneys of hares. Metal accumulation depends on age, season, sex and the degree of anthropogenic load. Muscle tissue is less contaminated than offal. The data obtained justify the need for mandatory postmortem veterinary and sanitary inspection of hare carcasses (including testing for trichinellosis, tularemia, toxoplasmosis), exclusion of liver and kidneys from the diet of animals from technogenic zones, and thorough thermal processing of the meat. Regular monitoring of hare populations as bioindicators of environmental pollution is recommended.

source_records.abstract: The hare is a popular hunting trophy, and its meat is widely consumed by hunters and their families, being perceived as an environmentally friendly product. However, fragmentary data on biological and chemical risks pose a threat to consumer health, necessitating a systematisation of information on the infectious, parasitic and toxicological aspects of hare meat safety. A search for relevant publications was conducted using keywords in Scopus, PubMed, eLibrary, Google Scholar and open Internet sources. Works containing data on zoonotic pathogens, helminths, coccidia, as well as on the content of heavy metals (Pb, Cd, Hg, Cr) and pesticides in hare tissues were analysed. The summarised data indicate that hares serve as a reservoir for Francisella tularensis, Yersinia spp., Toxoplasma gondii, Leishmania infantum, hepatitis E virus, as well as for helminths (Trichostrongylus spp. Protostrongylus spp., Taenia pisiformis) and coccidia. In industrially developed regions, exceedances of maximum permissible concentrations of lead (up to 3.53 mg/kg), cadmium (up to 49.12 mg/kg), mercury and chromium have been recorded in the liver and kidneys of hares. Metal accumulation depends on age, season, sex and the degree of anthropogenic load. Muscle tissue is less contaminated than offal. The data obtained justify the need for mandatory postmortem veterinary and sanitary inspection of hare carcasses (including testing for trichinellosis, tularemia, toxoplasmosis), exclusion of liver and kidneys from the diet of animals from technogenic zones, and thorough thermal processing of the meat. Regular monitoring of hare populations as bioindicators of environmental pollution is recommended.
